title: New Zealand finally wins a toss and opts to bowl in the 5th ODI against India
summary: New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner has finally won a toss and chosen to bowl in the fifth one-day cricket international against India at Bay Oval
story: New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner has finally won a toss and chosen to bowl in the fifth one-day cricket international against India at Bay Oval
MOUNT MAUNGANUI, New Zealand -- New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner has finally won a toss and chosen to bowl Sunday in the fifth one-day cricket international against India at Bay Oval.
India's captains Shubman Gill and Shreyas Iyer have won eight of nine tosses in previous matches in the Twenty20 and one-day international series.
When asked what he planned to do, Santner said “I'm unsure. I didn't expect to win (the toss).”

India captain Iyer said his team is still in “high spirits” after its defeat by 244 runs in the fourth ODI at the same venue Friday. New Zealand bowled out India for 89 in reply to its own 333. India still leads the five match series 2-1 after one match was washed out.

Matt Henry, who took the wickets of Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli and Iyer in his first over Friday and finished with 6-27, has left along with Kyle Jamieson to join the New Zealand squad for the first test which starts at Wellington on Thursday.
Jacob Duffy and Blair Tickner rejoin the New Zealand lineup for Sunday's match, bringing to nine the number of bowlers New Zealand has used in the series.
India has handed an ODI debut to right-arm pacer Yash Thakur while Mohammad Siraj also joins the India lineup.
Lineups:
New Zealand: Will Young, Tim Seifert, Nick Kelly, Dean Foxcroft, Finn Allen, Michael Bracewell, Mitchell Santner (captain), Kristian Clarke, Blair Tickner, Matt Fisher, Jacob Duffy.
India: Rohit Sharma, Ruturaj Gaikwad, Virat Kohli, Shreyas Iyer (captain), Ishan Kishan, Naman Dhir, Axar Patel, Auqib Nabi, Mohammed Siraj, Arshdeep Singh, Yash Thakur.

title: McDavid extends season-opening points streak to 21 games, Oilers beat Maple Leafs 1-0
summary: Connor McDavid extended his season-opening points streak to 21 games with an assist, Devon Levi made 20 saves for his first NHL shutout and the Edmonton Oilers beat Toronto 1-0 on Saturday night to hand the Maple Leafs their sixth straight home loss
story: Connor McDavid extended his season-opening points streak to 21 games with an assist, Devon Levi made 20 saves for his first NHL shutout and the Edmonton Oilers beat Toronto 1-0 on Saturday night to hand the Maple Leafs their sixth straight home loss

TORONTO -- Connor McDavid extended his season-opening points streak to 21 games with an assist, Devon Levi made 20 saves for his first NHL shutout and the Edmonton Oilers beat Toronto 1-0 on Saturday night to hand the Maple Leafs their sixth straight home loss.
Defenseman Evan Bouchard scored his 12th goal of the season for Edmonton (15-3-3). The Oilers are 7-1-1 in their last nine games.
McDavid picked up an assist to give him 50 points (11 goals, 39 assists) and add to his NHL lead.
Oilers coach Mike Babcock faced his former team in Toronto for the first time since being fired in November 2019.
Anthony Stolarz stopped 22 shots for Toronto (8-12-2), which suffered its sixth consecutive regulation loss to complete a disastrous six-game stretch at Scotiabank Arena.
The goaltender started consecutive games for the first time this season with Sergei Bobrovsky struggling to find traction after signing with the Maple Leafs in free agency on July 1.
Toronto dropped to 1-8-0 over its last nine.
Oilers: At Philadelphia on Sunday.
Maple Leafs: At Chicago on Tuesday night.

title: Stevenson, Alexander lead North Texas past South Alabama 66-65
summary: Je'Shawn Stevenson scored 26 points to lead North Texas and Aeneas Alexander provided the winning basket with 30 seconds remaining as the Mean Green knocked off the South Alabama Jaguars 66-65 on Saturday
story: Je'Shawn Stevenson scored 26 points to lead North Texas and Aeneas Alexander provided the winning basket with 30 seconds remaining as the Mean Green knocked off the South Alabama Jaguars 66-65 on Saturday

DENTON, Texas -- Je'Shawn Stevenson scored 26 points to lead North Texas and Aeneas Alexander provided the winning points with a layup with 30 seconds left as the Mean Green took down South Alabama 66-65 on Saturday.

Stevenson shot 9 of 21 from the field, including 7 for 17 from 3-point range, and went 1 for 3 from the line for the Mean Green (3-1). Alexander scored 23 points, going 9 of 15 from the floor, including 3 for 8 from 3-point range, and 2 for 3 from the line. Reece Robinson had nine points and shot 2 of 3 from the field and 4 for 6 from the line.
Stephen Williams led the way for the Jaguars (2-3) with 15 points, six rebounds, three steals and two blocks. South Alabama also got 15 points from Jalen Langsy. Samuel Shoptaw also had 15 points.

title: Wucherpfennig puts up 19 in Fairfield’s 63-60 win over NJIT
summary: Declan Wucherpfennig had 19 points in Fairfield’s 63-60 victory over NJIT
story: Declan Wucherpfennig had 19 points in Fairfield’s 63-60 victory over NJIT
FAIRFIELD, Conn. -- Declan Wucherpfennig had 19 points in Fairfield’s 63-60 victory over NJIT on Saturday.

Wucherpfennig added eight rebounds for the Stags (2-2). Cole Edelen scored nine points, going 3 of 9 (3 for 7 from 3-point range). Tony Williams shot 3 for 8, including 2 for 5 from beyond the arc to finish with nine points.
Mario Tatum Jr. finished with 13 points and eight rebounds for the Highlanders (1-5). Victor Vanderstraeten added 12 points and 12 rebounds for NJIT. Brandon Stores Jr. also had 12 points.

title: Dahle leads Weber State past Northern Arizona to tighten the race atop the Big Sky
summary: Nate Dahle threw for 229 yards and two touchdowns and Weber State upset Northern Arizona in a dramatic 25-21 win
story: Nate Dahle threw for 229 yards and two touchdowns and Weber State upset Northern Arizona in a dramatic 25-21 win
FLAGSTAFF, Ariz. -- Nate Dahle threw for 229 yards and two touchdowns and Weber State upset Northern Arizona in a dramatic 25-21 win on Saturday.
Spencer Ferguson ran for 125 yards on 20 carries and Noah Kjar had 135 yards receiving on nine receptions and a touchdown for Weber State.
Northern Arizona's Ty Pennington threw for 300 yards, a touchdown and two interceptions, the last one to end the game.
The Wildcats' win moves them into a second-place tie in the Big Sky Conference with NAU.
Weber State, ranked 18th in the Stats Perform poll, moved to 7-4, 6-2 with No. 5 NAU at 8-3, 6-2. First-place Montana State (10-1, 7-1) beat Northern Colorado.

Dahle's 25-yard touchdown pass to Tate Kjar near the midway point of the third quarter put the Wildcats ahead for good at 22-17. On the 2-point conversion attempt, a scrambling Dahle threw across the field and was intercepted by safety Braylon Singleton, who returned it 100 yards to reduce the Lumberjacks' deficit to 22-19.
On NAU's final drive, Porter Small intercepted Pennington to end the game.
The Wildcats are 3-1 after playing their fourth straight game against a nationally ranked team. They beat Idaho State and UC Davis and lost at Montana State.
NAU saw its five-game win streak end.
Weber State leads the series, 30-29.
Weber State: concludes the regular season on Saturday when it hosts Utah Tech.
Northern Arizona: ends the regular season when it hosts Northern Colorado on Saturday.

story: Elijah Mahi scored 26 points to lead the Santa Clara Broncos and Jake Ensminger secured the victory with a 3-pointer with 31 seconds remaining as the Broncos defeated the New Mexico Lobos 90-85

SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- Elijah Mahi scored 26 points to lead Santa Clara and Jake Ensminger sealed the victory with a 3-pointer with 31 seconds remaining as the Broncos knocked off New Mexico 90-85 on Saturday night.

title: Rainy and cold reception for No. 19 Mississippi at Oklahoma day later after travel issues
summary: The mood around Oklahoma's game against No. 19 Mississippi was a bit subdued when played a day late
story: The mood around Oklahoma's game against No. 19 Mississippi was a bit subdued when played a day late

NORMAN, Okla. -- The Sooner Schooner was parked on the sideline and there were swaths of empty seats when Oklahoma kicked off Sunday against No. 19 Mississippi after the Rebels didn't arrive in time to play the game as scheduled the previous day.
Oklahoma fans who braved rain and chilly temperatures booed loudly when the Rebels ran out on the field before the start of the game.
Ole Miss arrived in Oklahoma City on Saturday night. The FAA’s decision to ground all flights on Friday sent sports teams nationwide scrambling for new travel accommodations.
While some other games adjusted kickoff times, Mississippi-Oklahoma was the only FBS game pushed back a day until Sunday.
Oklahoma athletic director Roger Denny was upset with the decision, saying the Southeastern Conference threatened the Sooners with a forfeit if they didn't agree to play Sunday.

“I understand that difficult decisions sometimes must be made under extraordinary circumstances,” Denny said in a statement on Saturday. “Put simply, this decision isn’t fair to our athletes, our institution or to Sooner nation.”

Clint and Kelsey Epperson, with their son and a buddy, stood in a steady rain outside Gaylord Family-Oklahoma Memorial Stadium before kickoff. They drove three hours from Commerce in northeast Oklahoma — where baseball Hall of Famer Mickey Mantle grew up — to celebrate their son's 10th birthday.
They had bought game tickets in advance and paid $140 to stay in Norman an extra night.

“We were coming, no matter what,” said Clint Epperson, who agreed with Denny that SEC Commissioner Greg Stankey didn’t have enough consideration for the fans in changing the game. “We were an afterthought.”

On a normal game day, the streets outside the stadium are lined with tailgating fans. The mood was subdued Sunday, with a sprinkling of fans wandering around and tents and outerwear dominating the scene.

Oklahoma cut the prices of beer and other concessions to draw fans, and moved basketball and wrestling events to later in the day. Football tickets were available online for as low as $20 in the hours leading up to kickoff.

The temperature when the game started just after noon local time was 44 degrees with 19 mph wind gusts making it feel closer to freezing. The game had originally been scheduled for 3:15 p.m. Saturday, when it was about 10 degrees warmer.

Ole Miss officials insisted they did everything possible to avoid postponing the game, and had every intention to fly to Oklahoma on Friday night and play Saturday. They also reiterated Sankey’s remarks that the school's charter company could not accommodate a late Friday night departure after the stoppage was lifted.

“At that hour, due to the time required to rescreen the party and travel to the Tupelo airport, the crew’s duty time would have expired prior to departure,” Ole Miss said in its statement Saturday. “There were no other flight options at that point, and we determined it was too late to put our student-athletes on a bus trip of eight or more hours. In addition, the flight crew’s duty time restrictions prevented us from being able to fly out until Saturday afternoon at the earliest.”
Ken Gallon, a 20-year Sooners season ticket holder, drove three hours as usual for the game and, like most fans wandering around the stadium before kickoff, was draped in a jacket and a rain poncho.

“I have to agree with the (Oklahoma) AD,” Gallon said. “I think that the commissioner took into account Ole Miss’s whatever and did whatever they wanted and they certainly didn’t do what we wanted, which was play on Saturday.”

title: Deshaun Watson throws for 312 yards against his old team as the Browns rally past the Texans 27-24
summary: Quinshon Judkins barreled into the end zone from 5 yards out with 53 seconds remaining, and the resilient Cleveland Browns stunned the Houston Texans 27-24
story: Quinshon Judkins barreled into the end zone from 5 yards out with 53 seconds remaining, and the resilient Cleveland Browns stunned the Houston Texans 27-24
CLEVELAND -- Deshaun Watson can talk all he wants about how playing the Houston Texans is just another game.
His coach doesn’t quite believe him. Not after Watson's latest bit of last-minute thievery lifted the Cleveland Browns to a thrilling 27-24 win over the Texans on Sunday.
“I don’t care what he says,” coach Todd Monken. “This meant a lot.”
And, perhaps more important to Watson, it might also say a lot about a group that's turning last-minute stunners into a habit.
“Everything is in our hands,” Watson said.
Those hands are getting increasingly comfortable when things get tight.

The Browns improved to 6-4 by snapping a two-game losing streak, with all six wins coming by four points or fewer, and all of them featuring go-ahead, fourth-quarter drives by led Watson. Quinshon Judkins capped a rally from an early 17-point deficit when he barreled into the end zone from 5 yards out with 53 seconds remaining.
Asked how his team keeps finding ways to win, Monken just shook his head.

“I don’t have the end of the story,” the first-year coach said after the Browns improved to 4-0 at home for the first time since 1963. “I just know if our guys keep fighting, keep battling, keep scratching and clawing, they always have a chance.”
It helps that Watson has revived his career this season.

Four-plus years after being acquired from Houston in a staggering deal that seemed destined to be among the most franchise-crippling in league history due to Watson's injuries, ineffective play and off-the-field issues stemming from his time with the Texans, the 31-year-old is playing like the difference-maker the Browns have long needed at the game's most important position.
Watson passed for 312 yards, rushed for 50 more — including a high-stepping 6-yard touchdown run — and shook off a fourth-quarter interception to send the Browns into their bye week on a high.
“This is what I’ve been working on, working for, my whole career,” Watson said, later adding, “People create stories and narratives. But my actions speak louder than my words.”

Trailing by four with less than two minutes to go, Watson guided the Browns 49 yards in just three plays. An unnecessary roughness penalty on Houston cornerback Kamari Lassiter for hitting a defenseless Tylan Wallace moved the ball 15 yards.
“I don’t know what I’m supposed to do,” Lassiter said. “Am I supposed to let him catch it? I’m just trying to rip the ball out of his hands. We play a violent sport.”
A 30-yard catch-and-run by tight end Harold Fannin Jr. moved the Browns to the 5, and Judkins did the rest.
C.J. Stroud passed for 211 yards with three touchdowns and an interception for Houston (3-6), which looked unstoppable early and inept late.
Nico Collins caught nine passes for 94 yards and a score for the Texans, who began the season with Super Bowl aspirations but now have little margin for error after another baffling loss.
“We ain’t got no more time,” safety Calen Bullock said. “No time and no more excuses. Every game is a playoff game for us.”
Houston seemed poised to take another step toward digging out of the hole it created with an 0-4 start. The Texans were dominant during the opening 20 minutes.

Playing without edge rusher Danielle Hunter, three-time Pro Bowl guard Wyatt Teller and wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr., the defense harassed Watson while Stroud led an offense that ripped off big play after big play.
And then it all vanished. The Texans, who racked up 194 yards on their first three drives, managed just 96 the rest of the way.
“They've come back on a lot of teams this season and won a lot of games with two-minute drives,” Stroud said. “We knew what it was. We were just dead.”
Still, Houston appeared in position to pull it out after Stroud hit Dalton Schultz for an 11-yard touchdown with 9:20 to go. Cleveland's next two drives ended with a punt and a pick by Watson.
But when Houston's defense — thought to be the team's biggest strength — needed one more stop, it faltered again.
And the Browns and their quarterback, who may finally be shedding the “embattled” moniker that has followed him since he arrived in Cleveland, delivered again.
The player who seemed to be on the cusp of being run out of town is now a leading candidate for Comeback Player of the Year.

“Even three months ago, people wasn’t even talking about that,” Watson said. “Just again, another opportunity for me to prove myself right and prove everybody else wrong. I believe in myself, and I believe in the people around me, and I’m going to continue to do that.”
Texans: RB Woody Marks ran for 50 yards in little over a half before being placed in the concussion protocol in the third after absorbing a helmet-to-helmet hit.
Brown: DE Derek Barnett left in the first quarter with a hamstring injury.
Texans: Host Indianapolis on Thursday night.
Browns: Off next week, then welcome Las Vegas on Nov. 29.

title: Trevor Lawrence lights up the Titans as the Jaguars roll 40-23 for a sixth win in 7 games
summary: Trevor Lawrence threw for 352 yards and three touchdowns as the Jacksonville Jaguars beat the Tennessee Titans 40-23 Sunday for their sixth victory in seven games
story: Trevor Lawrence threw for 352 yards and three touchdowns as the Jacksonville Jaguars beat the Tennessee Titans 40-23 Sunday for their sixth victory in seven games
NASHVILLE, Tenn. -- Trevor Lawrence has found a way to play even better, and he's elevating the Jacksonville offense right along with him.
Lawrence threw for 352 yards and three touchdowns as the Jaguars beat the Tennessee Titans 40-23 on Sunday for their sixth victory in seven games.

“I wouldn’t just say this is the best I’ve ever seen him,” Jaguars wide receiver Parker Washington said. “I’m saying I always knew he could play at this level and, shoot, I feel like there’s more in the tank. And we all feel like that. So, I’m excited for him and he’s going to continue to keep balling.”

The Jaguars (7-2) also won a franchise-record fifth straight against their AFC South rivals, and this was their eighth win in 11 games in the series. Jacksonville has a four-game lead sitting atop the division as well.
Lawrence became the eighth-youngest in NFL history to reach 20,000 yards passing, at the age of 27 years and 40 days.
“Can’t say enough about how he’s playing right now,” Jaguars coach Liam Coen said.

He did it completing passes to nine Jaguars for the fourth-highest passing yardage total of his career. Lawrence has topped 300 yards passing in three of five games, and the Jaguars have scored at least 30 points in four straight games. That matches the franchise's longest such streak, first set in 2017 in Weeks 13-16.

“I just have a lot of comfort in what we’re doing, a lot of confidence,” Lawrence said of his second season with Coen. “I know what we’re doing. I feel like myself and our whole offense, but myself and the staff, like we’re all on the same page. I know what we’re trying to get done.”

Washington had a career-high 148 yards receiving by halftime and finished with 152. Cam Little kicked field goals of 46, 48, 36 and 40 yards. Bhayshul Tuten added a 6-yard TD run with 1:10 left, padding the score off Tennessee's turnover on downs.
Travis Hunter had an interception as the Jaguars held Tennessee to 327 yards of total offense even with new trade acquisitions safety Jessie Bates III and defensive tackle Jordan Davis inactive.

The depleted Titans (1-8) remain winless at home as they lost their fifth in their final season at Nissan Stadium. After trading their top two defensive players in tackle Jeffery Simmons and safety Amani Hooker, the Titans put two more on injured reserve Saturday in left guard Peter Skoronski and punter Tommy Townsend.

Tennessee scratched three more starters, with rookie wide receiver Carnell Tate and linebackers Cody Barton and rookie Anthony Hill Jr. sidelined by injuries. Chandler Zavala, signed from the practice squad Saturday, started at left guard.
“I thought our guys gave us everything they had,” Titans coach Robert Saleh said. “Unfortunately, they made more plays than we did.”
The Jaguars took the lead from the opening drive and never trailed after Lawrence hit Washington for a 2-yard TD.

Cam Ward found Elic Ayomanor for a 50-yard catch-and-run that was the longest completion of the quarterback's young career, and Ward capped the drive with a 2-yard TD pass to Daniel Bellinger, pulling the Titans within 13-10. Little's 36-yard field goal made it a 16-10 halftime lead.
Joey Slye kicked two of his three field goals in the second half to keep the Titans within range.

Jacksonville answered with a 10-play drive, capped by a 3-yard TD pass by Lawrence to Brenton Strange on fourth-and-2 at the Titans 3. Saleh was furious officials missed a pick on his defender, leaving Strange wide open for the TD catch and a 23-13 lead. Lawrence made it 30-16 with a 25-yard TD pass to Josh Cameron early in the fourth quarter.
The Titans answered with Tony Pollard taking a dump-off pass from Ward 32 yards to the end zone pulling them within 30-23 with 8:21 remaining. That was as close as they would get.
Jaguars DE Danny Striggow was evaluated for a concussion in the first half and did not return. Jaguars C Robert Hainsey hurt his left knee early in the third quarter and did not return.
Titans S Tony Adams suffered a concussion that sidelined him, and WR Wan'Dale Robinson hurt an ankle.
The Jaguars visit the New York Giants.
The Titans visit Dallas.

title: Dampier accounts for 4 TDs, No. 2 Utah remains undefeated with 40-39 win over No. 22 Arizona
summary: Devon Dampier hit Creed Whittemore on a 70-yard touchdown pass with 2:25 left, Daniel Bray ran for 197 yards and No. 2 Utah remained undefeated with a wild 40-39 victory over No. 22 Arizona early Sunday
story: Devon Dampier hit Creed Whittemore on a 70-yard touchdown pass with 2:25 left, Daniel Bray ran for 197 yards and No. 2 Utah remained undefeated with a wild 40-39 victory over No. 22 Arizona early Sunday
TUCSON, Ariz. -- Utah's day began with a morning flight that left a day late.
It ended with a wild win that leaves the Utes with a clear path to the College Football Playoff.

Devon Dampier hit Creed Whittemore on a 70-yard touchdown pass with 2:25 left, Daniel Bray ran for 197 yards and No. 2 Utah remained undefeated with a wild 40-39 victory over No. 22 Arizona early Sunday.

The Utes (10-0, 7-0 Big 12, No. 2 CFP) didn’t arrive in Tucson until just after noon due because of the FAA ground stop Friday and got off to a slow start, falling into an early 11-point hole in a game pushed back three hours to 8:30 p.m.
Dampier led Utah back, pulling out a win filled with obstacles — on the field and off — to stretch the Utes' winning streak to 16 games over two seasons.
“Our culture is no excuses. We live by it,” Dampier said. “No one’s going to feel sorry for us if we would’ve lost this game, so that was just kind of the mindset."

The Wildcats (7-3, 4-3, No. 23 CFP) pulled off a midnight miracle against TCU last week and found themselves in another late-night game against the highest-ranked opponent to play in Tucson since No. 2 Oregon in 2007.
A wild back-and-forth second half reminiscent of the Pac-12 After Dark days — Big 12 After Dark? — came down to which of the two star quarterbacks could come through.
Arizona's Noah Fifita did his part, throwing for 356 yards and three touchdowns. He hit Isaiah Mizell on two TDs, the second a 10-yarder that put Arizona up 39-33 with just over three minutes left.

“To me, this night, the way it went start to finish, speaks to our belief, our resilience and our response,” Arizona coach Brent Brennan said. “The way our guys responded all night I thought was really, really special.”
Dampier was just better.
He answered Fifita's last TD pass with his 70-yard pass to Whittemore and Utah's defense sealed it with a fourth-down stop, stretching its conference winning streak to 12 straight games.

Dampier finished with 204 yards and two touchdowns passing, but also threw an interception and lost a fumble. He ran for 100 yards and two more scores to put the Utes in prime position to reach the Big 12 title game and the CFP.
“What a crazy game,” Utah coach Morgan Scalley said. “We knew this wasn’t going to be an easy one.”
Utah's players had to endure a long day on Friday during the FAA shutdown, but did get a chance to sleep in their own beds.
Everyone was on time for the morning flight and, after a toast of cherribundi antioxidant juice on the plane, arrived in Tucson unnerved by the obstacles.

“It was like a high school game, honestly, taking it back to Friday nights,” said Whettemore, who had five catches for 92 yards. “It was just like getting on a bus and going and playing a game like in high school.”
Utah: The Utes survived one big test by beating rival BYU last week and pulled out another one to put themselves in position for a CFP bid.
Arizona: The Wildcats had won seven straight home games after the comeback against TCU last week, but came up just short in another game that carried over into the next day.
Utah: At TCU next Saturday.
Arizona: At Kansas State next Saturday.

title: Lions star Amon-Ra St. Brown wears lederhosen on arrival to Munich stadium for game vs Patriots

story: Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown tapped into his German roots by wearing lederhosen on his arrival at Allianz Arena for Sunday’s game against the New England Patriots
MUNICH -- Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown tapped into his German roots by wearing lederhosen on his arrival at Allianz Arena for Sunday's game against the New England Patriots.
Even though his mother is not from the region — she hails from Leverkusen — St. Brown and some teammates still got into the local custom by sporting the iconic Bavarian attire.
Lions long snapper Hogan Hatten and wide receiver Isaac TeSlaa also wore lederhosen — typically deer leather shorts with suspenders, and popular at Oktoberfest.

St. Brown, a fluent German speaker, was asked in German on Friday if he would use a traditional Bavarian folk dance called “schuhplattler” for a touchdown celebration. He said he hasn’t made any decisions yet.
Four years ago, an editor from German broadcaster ProSieben surprised Tom Brady at a press conference in Munich by presenting the then-Buccaneers quarterback with specially made lederhosen.

title: Auburn causes havoc to beat Mississippi State and become bowl eligible for first time since 2023
summary: Auburn recovered four fumbles that led to 24 points and earned bowl eligibility for the first time in three years in a 41-9 win over Mississippi State
story: Auburn recovered four fumbles that led to 24 points and earned bowl eligibility for the first time in three years in a 41-9 win over Mississippi State
STARKVILLE, Miss. -- Auburn recovered four fumbles that led to 24 points and earned bowl eligibility for the first time in three years in a 41-9 win over Mississippi State on Saturday.

State had positive momentum after Auburn (6-4, 4-4 Southeastern Conference) missed a 47-yard field goal midway through the second quarter and gave the Bulldogs (4-6, 2-6) the ball back down three. However, four plays later, A.J. Swann was strip-sacked and the ball was returned by Darrion Smith to the 1. Byrum Brown scored on Auburn’s next play to make it 17-7.
The strip sack was one of three by the Tigers.
Billy Puckett, in for an injured Swann, was the victim of Auburn’s third strip sack on the third play of State’s next drive. The Tigers recovered at the State 21 and went ahead 24-7 four plays later.
Kolin Wilson coughed up the ball with less than two minutes left before halftime, which gave the Tigers good enough field position to tack on a field goal before the break.

The dagger was delivered with 9:23 left in the third. Brown tossed one up 34 yards to Chas Nimrod, who jumped over a defender in the end zone and held onto it for the score. Keshaun Singleton added insurance with a 42-yard grab at the 5:52 mark to make it 41-7.
Auburn’s first strip sack of Swann put it at Mississippi State’s 38-yard line early in the first quarter. Facing pressure three plays later, Byrum Brown found Singleton for a 26-yard touchdown.

The Bulldogs drove deep into Tiger territory on their next drive, but Kyle Ferrie missed a field goal. Auburn responded with one of its own to make it 10-0 with 1:44 left in the opening quarter. State, however, found life when Swann found Sanfrisco Magee for a 34-yard score on the first play of the second.
Auburn: The Tiger defense caused havoc and created opportunities that the offense cashed in on.
Mississippi State: The Bulldogs’ offensive line could not hold up under pressure and most scoring opportunities they did have were squandered.
Auburn hosts Samford next Saturday.
Mississippi State hosts Tennessee Tech next Saturday. ___

title: Antetokounmpo scores 34, Heat block 14 shots and roll past Pistons 137-117 for 4th straight win
summary: Giannis Antetokounmpo had 34 points, 14 rebounds and eight assists, some of the spectacular variety, and the Miami Heat beat the Detroit Pistons 137-117 on Saturday night for their fourth straight win
story: Giannis Antetokounmpo had 34 points, 14 rebounds and eight assists, some of the spectacular variety, and the Miami Heat beat the Detroit Pistons 137-117 on Saturday night for their fourth straight win

MIAMI -- Giannis Antetokounmpo had 34 points, 14 rebounds and eight assists, some of the spectacular variety, and the Miami Heat beat the Detroit Pistons 137-117 on Saturday night for their fourth straight win.
Klay Thompson scored 26 points in his return from a sprained ankle and Bam Adebayo added 20 for the Heat. Davion Mitchell had 15 points and nine rebounds for Miami.
Cade Cunningham had 33 points and eight assists for Detroit, which got 20 points and seven assists from Kevin Huerter.
Miami had nine players record at least one block and finished with 14 as a team — one shy of the franchise record.

The NBA record for players on the same team having at least one block in a game is 10, done twice — both by Golden State, first in 1991 and then again in 2016. The Heat team record for players with at least one block was eight, done on five occasions.

Antetokounmpo finished a weekend where he scored 71 points in a two-day span, after finishing with 37 in Miami's win over Cleveland on Friday night. He also had a through-the-legs assist to Thompson for a 3-pointer in the opening quarter.
It was one of six 3s on the night for Thompson, who is now 26 away from tying former Heat guard Ray Allen (2,973) for the third-most 3-pointers in NBA history.

Miami won for the seventh time in its last nine games and became the fourth team in the last 25 seasons to start 0-4 but rally to a winning record at the 13-game mark. Sacramento (7-6) did it in 2022-23, Oklahoma City (8-5) did it in 2018-19 and Dallas (9-4) did it in 2006-07.
It also matched the best nine-game stretch for the Heat since an 8-1 burst in November 2023.

title: Cedric Coward has 23 points and 12 rebounds as Grizzlies beat Nets 129-110
summary: Cedric Coward had 23 points and 12 rebounds and Taylor Hendricks scored a career-high 22 as Memphis built an early lead and defeated the Brooklyn Nets 129-110 on Saturday night
story: Cedric Coward had 23 points and 12 rebounds and Taylor Hendricks scored a career-high 22 as Memphis built an early lead and defeated the Brooklyn Nets 129-110 on Saturday night
MEMPHIS, Tenn. -- Cedric Coward had 23 points and 12 rebounds and Taylor Hendricks scored a career-high 22 as Memphis built an early lead and defeated the Brooklyn Nets 129-110 on Saturday night.

A night after a 142-111 victory over New Orleans featured 10 Memphis players reaching double figures, tying an NBA record, seven Grizzlies reached double figures against the Nets. Javon Small scored 19 and Cam Spencer finished with 17 and eight assists as Memphis won its third in the last four.
Julius Randle lead Brooklyn with 22 points and Day’Ron Sharpe added 16 points and 11 rebounds as Brooklyn lost its third in the last four. Noah Clowney scored 15.

Memphis built a 20-point first-half lead behind 3-point success and weathered a third quarter Brooklyn burst that cut the advantage to single digits. By early in the fourth quarter, Memphis had taken the lead back to 24.

Both teams had to overcome travel issues out of New Orleans that plagued the country during Friday's grounding of planes. The Nets stayed over after playing New Orleans on Wednesday; the Grizzlies beat the Pelicans on Friday night.
The teams arrived midday Saturday only hours before tipoff. That led to compressed game preparation.

Then Brooklyn's leading scorer and rebounder Michael Porter Jr. was a late scratch for personal reasons, eliminating 21.5 points and 7.5 rebounds from the Nets arsenal. The Grizzlies were without starters Ty Jerome, the team's leading scorer, and center Zach Edey.

Memphis built an early double-digit lead behind starting 9 of 11 from 3-point range. The Nets shooting would improve in the second quarter, but Spencer's 3-pointer as time expired in the second — their 13th of the half — gave Memphis a 71-54 lead at the break.

title: Lamson and White lead Montana State over Northern Colorado 31-21
summary: Quarterback Justin Lamson runs for two touchdowns as Montana State beats Northern Colorado 31-21 on Saturday night
story: Quarterback Justin Lamson runs for two touchdowns as Montana State beats Northern Colorado 31-21 on Saturday night

title: Spanish club Tenerife pays tribute to Jesús de Miguel in its first match since soccer player's death
summary: Spanish soccer club Tenerife pays tribute to Jesús de Miguel in its first game since the striker’s shocking death
story: Spanish soccer club Tenerife pays tribute to Jesús de Miguel in its first game since the striker’s shocking death

MADRID -- Spanish soccer club Tenerife on Sunday paid tribute to Jesús de Miguel in its first game since the striker's shocking death, with midfielder Nacho Gil holding up De Miguel's jersey after scoring his team's opening goal shortly before halftime.

Before the second-division match, players from both Tenerife and Ceuta wore jerseys reading “Siempre en nuestro recuerdo” (Always in our memory). They gathered at midfield for a moment of silence. The shirts all had De Miguel's name and his No. 9 on the back.
After the warmup, Tenerife captain Enric Gallego placed De Miguel’s jersey on the field, and his teammates gathered around it.
Play stopped in the ninth minute, marking De Miguel's shirt number. Players, coaches and fans applauded.
Gil appeared overcome with emotion when he was given De Miguel's jersey after scoring in the 40th. Neal Viereck sealed Tenerife's 2-0 win over Ceuta, its first league victory since September.
A mural depicting De Miguel had been painted outside Gate 9 at Tenerife's Heliodoro Rodríguez López Stadium, where fans had left flowers, scarves and candles following his death.

De Miguel died on Nov. 3. He was chasing a high ball in midfield when he was struck in the chest by Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono, who rushed far outside his area near the end of the Nov. 2 match in Tenerife. The 30-year-old De Miguel suffered cardiac arrest following the collision.

Owono on Friday was suspended for 12 games after he received a red card for the on-field collision with De Miguel. The Spanish soccer federation’s disciplinary committee said Owono used “excessive force” in the collision.
Owono had issued a statement through his club expressing his remorse and offering his condolences to De Miguel’s family.

Spanish police opened an investigation into possible involuntary manslaughter. Under Spanish law, deaths from non-natural causes, including accidents, are subject to judicial investigation, though prosecutors have said that criminal proceedings were unlikely.
Andorra coach Carles Manso said Thursday that it would be up to Owono to decide when he feels ready to play again.

title: Scotland beats Australia in Nations Championship rugby in latest big win for the northern hemisphere
summary: Scotland has struck another big blow for the northern hemisphere in Nations Championship rugby by beating Australia 15-12 at Murrayfield
story: Scotland has struck another big blow for the northern hemisphere in Nations Championship rugby by beating Australia 15-12 at Murrayfield
EDINBURGH, Scotland -- Scotland struck another big blow for the northern hemisphere in Nations Championship rugby by beating Australia 15-12 in an attritional test match at Murrayfield on Sunday.
It came after France defeated world champion South Africa 21-19 on Friday and Wales beat New Zealand 35-28 on Saturday for a first win over the All Blacks in 73 years.
Scotland led 12-5 at halftime after scoring two tries — through flanker Matt Fagerson in the ninth minute and No. 8 Jack Dempsey in the 29th — either side of one by Australia winger Harry Potter.

A highly physical match passed by without a point scored for 46 minutes, before Scotland flyhalf Finn Russell booted a penalty in the 75th to leave Australia needing two scores to win and little time to do so.
Max Jorgensen scampered down the right wing in the 80th minute for a converted try and there was one final chance for Australia after the restart, also down Jorgensen’s flank.

Scotland winger Darcy Graham was there to make the decisive tackle and relief spread around Murrayfield for a third win in five matches by the Scots in the inaugural tournament taking place over July and November. They moved above Wales into fourth place in the northern hemisphere standings.
Australia, next year’s Rugby World Cup host, has four losses in its five outings so far and is fourth in the southern hemisphere table.
The sixth and final round of matches takes place on Saturday, before the playoff finals at Twickenham from Nov. 27-29.

title: Braden Frager scores a career-high 26 points in No. 25 Nebraska’s 102-75 win over Boise State
summary: Braden Frager scored a career-high 26 points and No. 25 Nebraska beat Boise State 102-75 at the Sanford Pentagon
story: Braden Frager scored a career-high 26 points and No. 25 Nebraska beat Boise State 102-75 at the Sanford Pentagon
SIOUX FALLS, S.D. -- Braden Frager scored a career-high 26 points and No. 25 Nebraska beat Boise State 102-75 Sunday at the Sanford Pentagon.
The Cornhuskers (4-0) never trailed and built the lead to as many as 28 in the second half.

Frager also had a game-high seven rebounds and was 8 for 11 from the field. The junior from Lincoln entered the game averaging 11.0 points per game but surpassed that in the first half on one of his three 3-pointers. His previous career high was 23 against Oregon last season.

Five different Nebraska players scored in double figures, including leading scorer Pryce Sandfort, who finished with 17 points. Sam Orme scored 15 while Cale Jacobson and Boden Kapke added 13 each. Orme hit three 3-pointers in just over two minutes midway through the second half.
The Cornhuskers held a 35-24 rebounding edge and outscored Boise State’s bench 33-8.

Boise State (3-1) entered the game as the nation’s leading scoring team at 114.3 points per game. The Broncos fell way short of that pace in the first half, shooting 39% and scoring a season low 34 points.
Aginaldo Neto and Spencer Ahrens scored 17 points each to lead the Broncos, who hit 13 3-pointers.

Nebraska began their surge for a big lead late in the first half. The Cornhuskers went on a 14-3 run in the final three minutes to close out the half, including an 8-0 spurt to build a 52-34 lead at the break after Sandfort scored with four seconds remaining. His four points in four seconds after a basket, stolen inbounds pass and ensuing layup helped fuel the 8-0 run to close out the half.
Boise State hosts Sam Houston on Friday night.
Nebraska hosts South Dakota on Wednesday night.

title: Ava Heiden's double-double helps No. 10 Iowa women beat eighth-ranked Vanderbilt 75-65
summary: Chazadi Wright scored 16 points, junior Ava Heiden had 15 points and 13 rebounds for her 10th career double-double and No. 10 Iowa beat eighth-ranked Vanderbilt 75-65 in the Bad Boy Mowers Series
story: Chazadi Wright scored 16 points, junior Ava Heiden had 15 points and 13 rebounds for her 10th career double-double and No. 10 Iowa beat eighth-ranked Vanderbilt 75-65 in the Bad Boy Mowers Series

SIOUX CITY, Iowa -- SIOUX CITY, Iowa (AP) — Chazadi Wright scored 16 points, Ava Heiden had 15 points and 13 rebounds for her 10th career double-double and No. 10 Iowa beat eighth-ranked Vanderbilt 75-65 on Sunday in the Bad Boy Mowers Series.
Iowa built an early 19-7 lead and led by double figures the rest of the way to stay in control of the top-10 matchup.

Vanderbilt missed its first 13 3-pointers before Aubrey Galvan sank a shot from distance with 7:11 left in the fourth. Mikayla Blakes made the second 3-pointer less than a minute later to get within 63-51 — the closest Vanderbilt had been since it was 21-8.
After the Commodores missed a wide-open layup that would have pull them within 10 points, Dani Carnegie made a long 3-pointer with 3:46 left for a 68-53 lead.
Iowa held Vanderbilt to 36% shooting (25 of 70) after the Commodores entered having scored 100 or more points in four straight games to begin the season.
Amari Whiting added 11 points and 12 rebounds for Iowa (4-1), which lost at then-No. 2 UConn last Sunday. Carnegie finished with 10 points.
Blakes scored 20 points on 6-of-22 shooting for Vanderbilt (4-1). Mia Woolfolk added 19 and Galvan scored 15.

Blakes has scored 10-plus points in 58 straight games — the third-longest active streak among all active NCAA Division I players. Its the longest double-digit scoring streak by a Commodore this century.
The Commodores had won 24 consecutive regular-season games against non-SEC teams.
Vanderbilt: Returns home to play North Alabama on Wednesday.
Iowa: Hosts Montana State on Thursday.

title: Fans cheer as popular online platform for spinoff stories nears full return after security incident
summary: The Archive of Our Own, a popular global fandom site, is making a limited return after a security incident led to a shutdown on Oct. 29
story: The Archive of Our Own, a popular global fandom site, is making a limited return after a security incident led to a shutdown on Oct. 29

In a comeback tale like one from Harry Potter battling back his nemesis or a “Heated Rivalry” hockey hero rebounding from injury, a top global fandom site that was sidelined by a security incident is now on the mend.

The activist group behind the popular Archive of Our Own, or AO3, platform, a collaborative online space which serves up fans’ spinoff narratives derived from well-known published stories, says it’s undergoing a limited return after a shutdown on Oct. 29.
“AO3 is now up!” said a status page for the Organization for Transformative Works, an activist group behind the platform, on Sunday.

The outage sent fans of the platform — readers and authors alike — into a desperate void for the past two weeks with a “Bad Gateway” message stirring frustration. The return drew many expressions of joy Sunday.

The organization, in a summary it posted on Instagram of its 2025 results, said nearly 2.6 million AO3 works were created, with nearly 40 billion page views. Nearly 2 million accounts have been created, it said.
AO3 hasn't been without its critics, who have warned about sexual content that could be available to minors and fandom racism through the platform.

The group said some features like user icons have been disabled and importing of external work isn’t available, while downloads are currently only possible in the web-language HTML format. It promised those features will ultimately return.

The team predicted that the security incident would take up to four weeks for AO3 to get back up, while floating the prospect of a partial revival “in a degraded state” — which appears to be what was taking place on Sunday.

The organization said contributors’ “works, bookmarks, kudos, etc., are still safe” and that no drafts were deleted during the outage — but it couldn’t rule out that the user database might have been compromised.
“We understand that the wait and uncertainty surrounding AO3’s return have been difficult, and we apologize for the inconvenience,” the status update said.

AO3 is a hub of content from fans who have produced content that riffs off fiction, art and other culture and entertainment: Imagine a repository of sequels, prequels and derivatives dreamt up by adoring aficionados of some of the world’s best-known titles.
The result is catchy products like “fanfic” — fiction from fans — and similar fanart, as well as “podfics,” readings of narratives shared in audio form.

A recent listing of “ship stats” — or the number of references to relationships of stars from literature — shows that pairings of characters featured in the Harry Potter, Heated Rivalry and anime fandoms were the most prominent this summer.
The reaction from fans of the fandom platform was swift and exuberant.
“So, we've all agreed we don't need to sleep tonight, now that AO3 is finally back, right? Right!?” quipped yet.another.loon on the Threads social media site.
User Verkielos gushed: “Just got email from AO3 about a fic update. The world is healing!”
Associated Press writer Stefanie Dazio in Berlin contributed to this report.

title: Megaspeed says Alice Huang left in 2025, company conducts probe over Nvidia fallout
summary: Singapore-based company has been at the center of the claims involving Nvidia.
story: Singapore-based company has been at the center of the claims involving Nvidia.

Singapore-based cloud computing company Megaspeed International said Sunday that Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, whose relationship with former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang sparked U.S. national security concerns, left the company last year.
Megaspeed, which is under scrutiny over alleged transfers of advanced Nvidia chips to Chinese companies, also announced an internal investigation led by outside lawyers.

The company told The Associated Press that it runs a “legitimate and lawful business” and was aware of media reports containing claims about its business, supply chain and global operations “that are not supported by verifiable evidence.” It did not address specific allegations.
“The company has retained external legal counsel to conduct a thorough internal investigation,” it said in an emailed statement.
Alice Huang “left Megaspeed effective Aug. 30, 2025, and currently has no role with the company,” the statement said. “Megaspeed does not comment on Ms. Huang’s personal and private matters.”

A customer and cloud partner of Nvidia, Megaspeed has faced scrutiny in recent months, including from U.S. authorities, over allegations that it circumvented U.S. export restrictions to route large quantities of advanced chips to Chinese companies. Last December, it said there was “no evidence” of illicit chip transfers.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Sunday that “it doesn't matter to me” whether Alice Huang is a spy. He said his concern is “whether Nvidia had a culture of compliance around the U.S. export restrictions” or not.

“Jensen’s foibles are his foibles. Obviously, it’s a problem if in fact he was having relationships with subordinates,” Bessent said in an appearance on Fox News Channel's “Sunday Morning Futures.” “I want to keep coming back to: ‘What was the culture at Nvidia, and were they pressing these seemingly illicit sales to goose their revenues and their earnings?’”
Bessent said the Nvidia board of directors should look outside the company for a new CEO because “they need a dramatic shake-up.”
Singapore’s government said Thursday that it initiated an investigation into Megaspeed in February 2025, including possible “false declarations in relation to the purchase of servers.”
Authorities also investigated Alice Huang, whom the government identified as Megaspeed’s then-CEO, chairperson and one of its key controllers.

Singapore authorities questioned her and withheld her passport last year. They later concluded there was insufficient evidence that she had committed a crime, despite suspecting she had provided “inaccurate” information to downplay her role at the company.
An earlier New York Times report suggested U.S. officials believed Alice Huang was a Chinese spy recruited to potentially influence Nvidia to make its advanced chips more available to China.
As scrutiny intensified and reports of her romantic relationship with Jensen Huang gained attention, Nvidia announced Thursday that he was stepping down as CEO.

U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche said Thursday, however, that the Justice Department had not concluded whether Alice Huang was a Chinese spy. Asked whether she was a spy, President Donald Trump said: “I don’t know if that’s been determined yet.”
Beijing rejected the allegations as unsubstantiated.
The Associated Press has been unable to reach Alice Huang for comment.

Megaspeed began as the overseas arm of a Chinese video game developer and was incorporated in Singapore in 2015 as 7Road International. It adopted its current name in March 2023, when all its shares were transferred to Huang Le Limited, a British Virgin Islands company. Alice Huang is also known by her Chinese name, Huang Le.
By November 2023, she was no longer listed as a Megaspeed director, and all her shares had been transferred to an entity owned by Singaporean businessman Tan Yong Pong, also known as James Tan.

Despite those public records, short seller Culper Research cited a Megaspeed employee in a report released this May as saying Alice Huang was “actually still our boss” and remained involved in daily operations.
The company’s finances have also attracted attention. Singapore corporate records show its total assets rose roughly 90-fold from end-2023 to 2024, reaching almost $3 billion.
In a separate statement Thursday issued under James Tan’s name, Megaspeed said it takes its obligations under U.S. export control laws “extremely seriously.”
The company said it had cooperated with inspections by the U.S. Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security and was ready to cooperate fully with other relevant U.S. authorities.

title: Microsoft says services fully restored after hourslong global outage
summary: Microsoft says services are fully restored after a massive, global outage that lasted for hours
story: Microsoft says services are fully restored after a massive, global outage that lasted for hours
Microsoft said Saturday that services were fully restored after a massive outage that lasted for hours.
“We have completed our efforts to address the underlying issue of the incident and restored service to the remaining impacted customers and regions,” the company said in an update on X.

Users reported that Microsoft 365 services, including Outlook, Teams and AI assistant Copilot, were interrupted. Downdetector, an online tracker, said it received outage reports from users in more than 70 countries and territories.

The outage affected governments, courts, healthcare services, businesses, airlines and banks in many places. Governments including those of Japan, Singapore and Australia reported that the hourslong episode had impacted some of their operations.
Over 430 million people use Microsoft 365 apps, Microsoft said on its website. Problems started appearing around midday Thursday in the U.S.
The Redmond, Washington-based company apologized on Friday for the disruptions and said the outage was “not related to cyber” or artificial intelligence agents.
It said the incident “was introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced” following a recent network change.

The disruptions offer the latest example of the cascading problems that can erupt when so many communications and technology platforms depend on the same provider. Some lawmakers outside the U.S. have also argued that the outage shows the consequences of overreliance on American tech.
“With no emails coming or going, many office workers feel like they are having a virtual snow day,” said Jeremy Singer, a professor at the University of Glasgow’s School of Computing Science.

Still, he added, “this problem serves to emphasize the dependence we have built on one company’s digital infrastructure, and may lead us to question whether we need more resilience in our IT ecosystem.”

The global reach of the outage was swift. After problems first emerged midday Thursday in the U.S., online tracker Downdetector said it received outage reports from 74 countries and territories within an hour.
The total number of people affected was not clear, but Microsoft said in January it had more than 450 million paid commercial subscriptions to its 365 services.

A series of posts by Microsoft 365 on X suggested its engineers struggled to get the problem under control for some time, drawing teasing from other companies and users alike. But the tech giant has said there is “no indication” that the disruptions were caused by malicious activity, specifically noting Friday that the outage was not related to a cyberattack or artificial intelligence agents.
Microsoft said a technical issue arose during an upgrade that followed “a recent network change.” The company added that it restored services gradually, which took longer.
As Microsoft addressed issues affecting its Exchange Online mailboxes, it earlier cited a failure that it said caused a number of its servers to be “unexpectedly unavailable” during automated checks.
For Outlook, many users said they couldn’t send or receive emails, or had trouble loading their inboxes altogether. Those problems piled up across much of the world into Friday.
In Britain, the outage brought a halt to a trial in Manchester. Judge Maurice Greene sent jurors home because of delays that he said illustrated the danger of the court’s reliance on technology.
The British government said it was “working closely” with Microsoft to assess any impact on public services but that “robust contingency plans” were in place to minimize disruption.

British police said they were unable to receive crime reports online and urged people to phone in urgent requests. The outage also affected some law enforcement in the U.S. The sheriff’s office in Colorado’s Arapahoe County, for example, noted that online bond payments were affected.

Also in Britain, the National Pharmacy Association warned customers of delays in getting medication. The outage affected the National Health Service and threatened to prevent doctors from emailing prescriptions to pharmacies.
“Please bear with your pharmacy teams today, where waits may be longer than normal and there may be delays to some prescriptions,” a spokesperson said.
Governments in Singapore, Japan, Greece and Norway said the outage affected some of their operations, including email communications for certain ministries or agencies.

And of course, businesses were wracked with disruptions. Hong Kong businessperson Danny Lau, who runs an aluminum company, said his business couldn’t receive updates from its U.S. customers through Outlook.
Some banks in Hong Kong, an Asian financial hub, also saw disruptions.

OpenAI and Anthropic reported problems connecting with Microsoft 365 tools, underscoring the ripple effects as more people use artificial intelligence platforms to interact with other companies’ software.

title: SpaceX’s Starship soars into orbit after booster explosion prevents an unprecedented double catch
summary: SpaceX has lost out on its attempt to recover its entire Starship back at the Texas launch pad
story: SpaceX has lost out on its attempt to recover its entire Starship back at the Texas launch pad

SpaceX's attempt to recover its entire Starship back at the launch pad was thwarted when the booster fell into the Gulf of Mexico and exploded Friday, but the spacecraft still soared into orbit in its boldest test yet.

Instead of returning to its Texas pad following liftoff, the first-stage booster was diverted to a point offshore. Despite the setback, the spacecraft continued on its way. It will steer toward the pad Saturday, barring further trouble. The flight could last as long as 22 hours.

It’s the first time that Starship will try to return to the pad from orbit, to be plucked in midair by mechanical arms secured to the launch tower. The loss of the booster meant Elon Musk's company missed out on a double catch.

The original goal was to retrieve every single piece of the rocket for the purpose of future recycling, something yet to be achieved anywhere in the world. Musk sees this leading to the kind of fast and consistent launch rates necessary for building moon bases and sending people to Mars.

Shortly after reaching orbit, Starship dropped off 26 of the company’s most advanced Starlink satellites. The plan is for Starship to complete 15 laps around the world at an altitude of around 170 miles (275 kilometers) before heading back to the launch site for Saturday’s grand finale.
SpaceX had already made three booster grabs at the company’s sprawling Starbase near the U.S.-Mexico border. That made Friday's miss all the more surprising.

“Well, that certainly isn’t the news that we had hoped to hear for today,” observed SpaceX launch commentator Kate Tice, adding that it was in line with the many rigorous safety checks to protect the pad. No explanation was provided for what went wrong.

This was the first attempt to capture the upgraded version of the booster that stretches 236 feet (72 meters) — the production model for moon and Mars expeditions. It will also be the first time the company attempts to catch the spacecraft, which spans 171 feet (52 meters). Together, they form the world’s biggest and most powerful rocket — an astounding 407 feet (124 meters) in height.

The spacecraft portion of the 14 previous Starships ended up in the ocean, either by design at flight’s end or by accident in a stream of flaming wreckage. During the first full-scale test flight in 2023, multiple engines failed to ignite and the tumbling rocket’s self-destruct system was activated.
The last test, in September, was the first to reach orbit, but SpaceX did not try to recover any of the rocket stages.

SpaceX plans to start launching Starships from Florida within a few months and from Louisiana in a few years. Scaled-up infrastructure, combined with full rocket reusability, is “how you go from zero launches to 10 to 100 to 1,000 to 10,000 to 100,000,” SpaceX’s Kiko Dontchev, vice president of launch, said at a NASA tech summit last week at Florida’s Kennedy Space Center.

SpaceX’s smaller Falcon rockets will continue to fly from Cape Canaveral, carrying astronauts to the International Space Station for NASA and from California carrying Starlinks. Satellites also will keep hitching Falcon rides for now. Musk wants Starships to eventually replace Falcons.

Falcon rockets “are still not fully reusable. We still throw that second stage away every single flight. Starship, we’re going to catch both the first stage and second stage,” Dontchev said ahead of Friday's launch.

NASA is paying SpaceX billions of dollars to land Artemis astronauts on the moon with Starships. Jeff Bezos’ Blue Origin is the other major player. NASA expects to decide a year before the Artemis IV lunar landing — the first by astronauts in more than half a century — whether to get the moonwalkers to the surface with Musk’s Starship or Bezos’ Blue Moon.

During next summer’s Artemis III mission, astronauts will practice docking their capsule with a Blue Moon and then a Starship in orbit around Earth. That will set the stage for an Artemis moon touchdown as early as 2028.
“We are looking forward to some of that on-orbit Starlink capability on Artemis III,” NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman said via X after Starship reached orbit.

title: Meta fined $887M in Italy over Android gallery photos, videos on Facebook
summary: Meta violated a European privacy directive incorporated into Italian law.
story: Meta violated a European privacy directive incorporated into Italian law.

ROME -- Italy announced an €805 million ($887 million) fine against Meta on Saturday for using photos and videos from Android users’ galleries on Facebook without specific consent or adequate disclosure.

The Italian Data Protection Authority said the feature, called “Get suggestions from gallery when browsing Facebook,” violated a European privacy directive incorporated into Italian law. The directive protects smartphones as part of a person’s private sphere and requires “free and informed consent” for such access, the authority said.
Investigators found that the feature was enabled by default and that Facebook requested gallery access through a single permission covering multiple app functions with different purposes.
The authority gave Meta 60 days to disable the feature and seek separate consent for its use. Italy has about 20 million Android users, the agency said.
Meta made no immediate comment.
The fine was imposed on Meta Platforms Ireland Limited, which challenged Italy’s jurisdiction, according to the statement.
The authority said Meta’s “lack of cooperation” with the investigation factored into the penalty, which amounts to approximately 0.47% of the group’s global turnover.

title: SpaceX’s Starship returns from orbit, caught by launch pad arms in dramatic first
summary: It was the grand finale that Elon Musk and his team hoped for.
story: CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla. -- SpaceX’s Starship made a triumphant return to Earth on Saturday, caught in midair by giant mechanical arms where its journey began 22 hours earlier.

It was the grand finale that Elon Musk and his team hoped for — the first-ever capture of a Starship flying back from space. But with the first-stage booster exploding shortly after Friday’s liftoff from Texas, the company fell short of its desired double catch, still the goal for accelerating moon and Mars travel.
Wreckage remained in the Gulf of Mexico, cordoned off by buoys, as the stainless steel, bullet-shaped spacecraft lowered itself upright at the launch pad.
The dramatic, sci-fi-like capture helped blot out the booster’s messy miss. Cameras panned the spacecraft up and down as it hung high above the ground, supported by the arms of the launch tower.
“Can you believe it?” SpaceX commentator Dan Huot shouted, dragging out each word. “Look at her! Baby, she’s back!”
Calling it an “epic day,” Musk later ascended the launch tower to take up-close video with his phone. He even hugged the spacecraft. “Looks great,” he reported via X.

SpaceX officials said Saturday’s catch demonstrates the full reusability of Starship, crucial for rapid and low-cost recycling. Although Friday’s booster recovery failed, the company had already made three previous booster catches, validating the technique.

NASA welcomed Saturday’s news. The space agency is paying billions of dollars for Starship to land Artemis astronauts on the moon later this decade and help build a permanent lunar base. Musk’s ambitions are even grander: He wants to launch a fleet of Starships to build a city on Mars.
“It was almost magic,” NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman said via X. “Making more believers by the day ... one step closer to (emojis of the moon and the U.S. flag)."

The world’s largest and most powerful rocket — a 407-foot (124-meter) behemoth — blasted off late Friday afternoon from SpaceX’s Starship base near the U.S.-Mexican border. Separating neatly from its booster before things went awry, the upper-stage spacecraft soared into orbit and released 26 advanced Starlink satellites.

Starship continued circling the world 165 miles (265 kilometers) up, with live views of itself and Earth streaming down via Starlink. The spacecraft completed 14 laps around Earth, outshining the previous mission’s one to two laps.
It was SpaceX’s 15th flight of a full-scale Starship since 2023 and its only second trip to orbit.
SpaceX reported that everything on the spacecraft, including its vital heat shield, appeared to work well.

As for the booster, SpaceX’s Kate Tice said its engines stopped firing too soon on the way back down. The booster’s guidance system sensed it wasn’t in the right position and automatically initiated the watery detour and self-destruction. Engineers are still investigating the cause.

SpaceX expects to begin launching Starships from Florida’s Kennedy Space Center within the next few months. That is the starting point for NASA’s next Artemis mission, which will skip the moon and remain in orbit around Earth for lunar lander practice.

Artemis III’s four astronauts will attempt to dock their capsule with not only Starship but Blue Origin’s Blue Moon. The two companies will take turns delivering crews to the lunar surface. NASA is targeting as soon as 2028 for Artemis IV, humanity’s first moon landing since the Apollo era more than half a century ago.
