title: The biggest move of the NFL trade deadline paid immediate dividends
summary: Making his first start for the Minnesota Vikings since 2023, quarterback Kirk Cousins picked up where he left off — almost literally.
story: Making his first start for the Minnesota Vikings since 2023, quarterback Kirk Cousins picked up where he left off — almost literally.
Cousins led the Vikings to a 30-10 victory over the Green Bay Packers on Sunday, ending Minnesota’s two-game losing streak and improving the team’s record to 7-2.
Cousins’s most recent start for the Vikings prior to Sunday also came at Green Bay. It was in 2023, and he tore his Achilles during that game, and Minnesota moved on from him the following offseason.

The Vikings have been looking for an answer at quarterback since, and they eventually came back around to Cousins at this year’s trade deadline. Cousins got the start Sunday only five days after he was acquired from the Las Vegas Raiders, and he made some big throws as he led Minnesota to its highest scoring output since Week 1.
“I didn’t even know what my code was to get into the building on Wednesday,” Cousins said postgame. “It took a village. I’m just grateful for all the people that stepped up to help.”

Cousins finished the game completing 21 of 31 passes for 207 yards, with two touchdowns and one interception. While his stats weren’t spectacular, he made a meaningful impact on money downs, as the Vikings finished the game converting eight of 16 on third down. (Entering Sunday, Minnesota was ranked 30th in third-down conversion percentage at 33.3%.)

Minnesota’s first touchdown came on a third and 23, as Cousins made a beautiful, drop-in-the-bucket throw to Myles Price, who bounced off defenders en route to the end zone. Cousins described it as a “big-time” play by Price.

Cousins made another great throw on a third-and-long later in the game, connecting with Tai Felton on a wheel route on a third and 15 in the second quarter. The pass set up a one-yard touchdown run on the next play.
Later, after the Packers had cut the Vikings’ 20-0 lead to 20-10, Cousins picked up another massive first, checking into a screen pass on third and 12 and finding Justin Jefferson for a first down.
“It was fun, it felt like old times watching Justin do what he just did on that play,” Cousins said. “It was like, ‘I remember that guy. He’s pretty special.’”
Five plays later, Cousins threw his second touchdown of the game and effectively iced any chances of a Green Bay comeback.

“[He] just brought a certain amount of poise, leadership, execution,” head coach Kevin O’Connell said postgame. “Ran the show incredibly clean. Can’t say enough about him, I know everybody in the organization felt it this week.”
For Subscribers
Jefferson, one of the game’s top receivers, was perhaps the biggest individual beneficiary of his old quarterback’s return. Jefferson’s nine receptions and 13 targets were both season highs.
For Subscribers

Though Cousins didn’t exactly light the box score on fire, his presence Sunday made Minnesota’s championship formula incredibly clear: Play lights out defense, and do just enough on offense with above-average quarterback play.

With Cousins helping push the Vikings out to an early lead, Minnesota’s defense pinned its ears back and got after Jordan Love. The Vikings finished the game with eight sacks, and limited the Packers to only 56 yards rushing.
Love, one of the game’s great deep-ball throwers, finished the game with 220 yards, his fewest since Week 4. His 46.6 QBR was also his third-worst mark of the season.
“For one of the first times this year, I thought we played complementary football,” O’Connell said.

The win was an important one for Minnesota. The Vikings are now two games clear of Green Bay in loss column in the loaded NFC North, and now also own the tiebreaker between the two teams. Minnesota kept pace with the Detroit Lions and Chicago Bears, both of whom are also 7-2.

The Vikings’ offense didn’t necessarily look perfect Sunday. But their quarterback making big throws and providing a steady hand while the defensedefense continued to dominate showed exactly why Minnesota decided to bring Cousins back.

title: 2 injured after taxiing planes collide at Miami International Airport
summary: Two taxiing planes collided at Miami International Airport on Saturday night, officials said, a day after a nationwide ground stop disrupted flights across the country.
story: Two taxiing planes collided at Miami International Airport on Saturday night, officials said, a day after a nationwide ground stop disrupted flights across the country.

At about 9 p.m. ET Saturday, the wing tip of a Copa Airlines Boeing 737 struck the nose of a UPS Boeing 767 as both aircraft were taxiing, according to a statement from the Federal Aviation Administration.

The Copa plane was taxiing to the gate, while the UPS plane was departing for Bogota, Colombia, the FAA said. The Copa flight had six crew members and 166 passengers aboard at the time of the collision, according to a statement from the airline.
Greg Chin, a spokesperson for the Miami-Dade Aviation Department, said in a statement that two people were treated at the scene for minor injuries and were not hospitalized.
The FAA said air traffic controllers had told the UPS crew to give way to the Copa flight.

UPS said in a statement that it was aware of the incident and “committed to working with authorities to determine what happened.” “The safety of our employees and the public is our highest priority,” the company said.
For Subscribers

The collision came a day after the FAA issued a rare nationwide ground stop because of a widespread air traffic control telecommunications issue. The ground stop lasted more than four hours and led to thousands of flight cancellations and delays. Officials believe a router problem during routine work was the cause of the outage.
For Subscribers
As of 10:20 a.m. ET Sunday, 1,583 flights within, into or out of the U.S. had been canceled, and another 2,944 were delayed.
Last year, 15 people were killed when a UPS cargo plane crashed just outside of Louisville, Kentucky’s Louisville Muhammad Ali International Airport.

title: Could a viral teen comedy be Netflix’s answer to YouTube?
summary: Netflix is hoping Gen Z audiences stream “Minimum Wage,” which began as a web series in 2024.
story: LIVERPOOL, N.Y. — Inside a make-believe pizza shop overlooking Onondaga Lake, a team of digital creators, filmmakers and young actors spent months cooking up a show that they hope will serve Netflix something it craves: a fresh audience.
“Minimum Wage,” a mockumentary that follows teens who work at a pizza shop, has garnered more than 30 million views across YouTube, TikTok and Instagram since launching in May 2024.
Now, Netflix is betting that Gen Z audiences will watch the viral hit in its expanded form on the streaming giant — and pay to view it.

The media company’s decision to acquire the show reflects a broader shift in Hollywood’s battle for younger viewers, as streamers increasingly turn to internet creators and their built-in fan bases to drive subscriptions and engagement.

Of course, it’s not a new strategy. For years, the industry has tried to tap into YouTube’s massive roster of creators. Sometimes, it’s a success: Amazon Prime’s reality competition series with YouTuber MrBeast, for example, became the platform’s most streamed unscripted series of all time. Other times, however, it’s more of a bust — like Netflix’s “Haters Back Off,” a comedy series with former YouTube star Colleen Ballinger, aka Miranda Sings, which was canceled after just two seasons.

But there has been a noticeable uptick in creator content across streaming in 2026. According to data from London-based market research firm Ampere Analysis, first published in Puck, creator-led programming across 16 U.S. streaming services surged more than 300% in the third quarter of 2026 compared with the same period a year earlier.

“YouTube is not just UGC [user-generated content] and cat videos anymore,” Netflix co-CEO Ted Sarandos said during the 2025 fourth quarter earnings call. “They are TV. So we all compete with them in every dimension for talent, for ad dollars, for subscription dollars and for all forms of content.”

With “Minimum Wage,” showrunner writer and executive producer Will Phelps said his agent at UTA “called up all the different streamers, and a couple different streamers wanted it … so we got multiple offers.”

He did not disclose which streamers were vying for the show’s rights. But in the end, Phelps said, Netflix emerged as the strongest partner for American High Shorts, the production company behind the project.
“We wanted to do it the way we were doing it on YouTube, but just on a bigger scope,” said Phelps, who co-showruns with Jeremy Garelick and Axelle Azoulay.
“And rather than pushing us to do something glossy and different, Netflix let us do what we do best,” Phelps added. “Except for now, we have a huge platform.”
Phelps, Garelick and Azoulay were able to retain creative control over the writing and directing.
And Netflix allowed the original cast of largely unfamiliar faces to stay on — including Grace Reiter, who recently joined “Saturday Night Live.”
Comedian Randall Park was also added to the ensemble, playing Terry Sylvester, founder, CEO and franchise owner of the struggling Slice Club pizzeria chain.
Episodes are typically between 12 and 20 minutes in length, as opposed to the traditional 30-minute sitcoms that populate network television.

Phelps, a veteran of the entertainment industry, said he believes the key to making a quality show is maintaining the elements of a strong story, while tailoring the format to the viewer’s attention span.
Recent data from UCLA’s Center for Scholars & Storytellers (CSS), a nonprofit research center, supports his assertion.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
Nearly 4 in 5 of the 1,500 survey respondents ages 10-24 said short-form videos can tell a story, according to the fifth annual “Teens and Screens” report, which was published in October.
While older generations identify storytelling with books, TV and movies, the same boundaries do not exist for younger generations, the report found.
“This is the first generation to grow up on video-first platforms, so for them short, creator-driven video simply is television,” Yalda T. Uhls, founder and CEO of CSS, told NBC News in an email.
For shows like “Minimum Wage” to succeed on streaming, young audiences have to find it authentic.
Thus far, the show has picked up buzz among viewers. The week the show launched, it was in the global top 10 of shows on Netflix, placing sixth behind Season 11 of “Love is Blind.”

Critics have also praised it — helping it notch a fresh score of 81% on the Rotten Tomatoes Tomatometer. One reviewer described the series as Gen Z’s version of “The Office,” NBC’s hit mockumentary sitcom that was set at the fictional Dunder Mifflin Paper Company in Scranton, Pennsylvania.

“A show like ‘Minimum Wage’ arrives with proof that an audience already loves it,” Uhls said. “The key is to bring over what made it work, meaning the creator’s voice and its authenticity, instead of polishing it into something generic.”

title: Sen.-elect Scott Colom says investing in the South can help Democrats win ‘a durable majority’
summary: Sen.-elect Scott Colom, D-Miss., emphasized in that Democrats need to invest more in southern states like Mississippi, where he flipped the seat blue for the first time in decades.
story: Sen.-elect Scott Colom, D-Miss., emphasized on NBC News’ “Meet the Press” that Democrats need to invest more in Southern states like Mississippi, where he flipped a seat blue for the first time in decades.
“What we need to do now as a Democratic Party is understand we can’t continue to allow that lack of investment to occur,” he said Sunday.

Colom’s projected win this month brought Democrats to a 55-seat majority in the Senate, with Alaska’s Senate race yet to be called. His victory over Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith, a Republican, marked a seismic political shift in a state that last elected a Democrat to the Senate 44 years ago and has not had a Black senator since the Reconstruction period.
Colom has been vocal in calling for Democrats to focus more on states like Mississippi, a view he emphasized again on Sunday.

“We need to put senators like myself in positions where we can deliver for the rural South, where we can be leaders in ways that show the voters in rural America that we care about them, the voters in the Deep South that we want them to be successful,” Colom said.
“And if we do that, I think we can have a competitive elections every cycle and put ourselves in positions where we can have a durable majority,” he continued.
In the same interview, Colom identified reshaping tariff policies as his top priority to reduce prices.

“We’ve got to fight for low tariffs to lower costs that helps our farmers, because they lost customers as a result of these tariffs, and we need to do everything in our power to help them get those customers back,” Colom said.
He also called for raising the minimum wage. The federal minimum wage sits at $7.25 per hour, and it has not been raised since 2009.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

NBC News exit polls indicated that the cost of living was a top priority for voters. NBC’s exit polls showed that 89% of voters considered the cost of living “crucial” or a “major factor” in thinking about their vote for Congress. The same exit polls found that 66% of voters believed Trump’s tariff policies hurt the national economy.

Colom was also asked on “Meet the Press” about whether he would vote to restore nationwide rights to abortion. The Mississippi senator-elect has said he is “personally pro-life because I’m a Christian” and that he does not “believe in late-term abortions.” He also said he does not believe that victims of rape or incest should be “forced” to “have that child.”
“I’ll study what’s right for my values and for Mississippi and try to represent those values in D.C. to the best of my abilities,” he said.

One of the tasks remaining for Congress this year is for Democrats to select their party leadership. Sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md., announced last week that he would challenge Sen. Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., for the Senate majority leader position.
Asked whom he planned to support, Colom said he was “in listening mode” and did not commit to either candidate.

“I don’t know either one of them that well, so I’m going to listen to what other people tell me about them, and I’m going to figure out what are the things that people are doing well in leadership, what are the things they’re not doing well, and find out how we can work together to achieve results,” Colom said.

title: Transportation secretary says he doesn’t apologize for FAA’s nationwide ground stop
summary: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy declined to apologize for the nationwide ground stop that stranded hundreds of thousands of travelers across the country
story: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy on Sunday declined to apologize for the nationwide ground stop on Friday that stranded hundreds of thousands of travelers across the country following a router issue that derailed air traffic control communications.
Instead, the secretary blamed his predecessors and previous presidential administrations that he said did not do enough to modernize the nation’s air traffic control system.

“It happened on my watch, but we have to be clear: I am moving at an incredible speed that no one has done at the FAA or in decades, and I’m proud of the work we’re doing, the attention we’re bringing to this issue,” Duffy told NBC News’ “Meet the Press.” “But I can’t apologize for what was passed off to us, and I can’t blame Republicans or Democrats because it’s all of them.”
The secretary also blamed “30 years of a lack of investment” from the country’s previous leaders.
“Why they didn’t do that I don’t know, but they gave me a system that needs to be fixed, and President [Donald] Trump and I are going to fix it,” he added.

His remarks come less than two days after the Federal Aviation Administration issued a national ground stop that lasted several hours, leading to thousands of flight cancellations beginning on Friday and continuing through the weekend.

FAA contractor L3Harris was working on replacing a copper line with a fiber line at a remote site when the work led a router to overwhelm the national FAA telecommunications network, Duffy said Saturday.
Duffy also said Sunday on “Meet the Press” that he expects airports and airlines to resume normal operations by the end of the day or early Monday morning.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
“By the end of today, into tomorrow, I think we’ll be back to normal,” he said, adding that Friday’s ground stop led airplanes and flight crews to be “out of position.”
“It takes some time for the airlines to rechoreograph all of their crews and aircraft. We’re going to start seeing things get better today, but I think back to normal tomorrow,” Duffy said.
The secretary also demurred when asked whether he could guarantee that a similar travel disruption won’t happen in the future.

“First we have to figure out what happened. Was this a faulty installation by L3Harris that was doing their work for us? Was it a fault of the router itself? We have to do that investigation and make sure we take precautions. We don’t want to shut down the airspace,” Duffy told “Meet the Press” moderator Kristen Welker.
“We’re going to figure out what was the root cause and then move forward from there, fixing how we do business at the FAA,” he added.
Duffy also reiterated a call he’s made all weekend for more funding from Congress to modernize the nationwide air traffic control system, which has long been outdated and faced problems.

“The president, since he came to office, has been pushing for modernization of the airspace. Before I was even sworn in, he brought this up,” the secretary said, pointing to $12.5 billion that was allocated for air traffic control improvements in a GOP-backed spending bill last year.

“The Congress was very specific in how I spend that money. I have a certain allotment for radar, a certain allotment for radios, a certain allotment for building new infrastructure for my centers for air traffic controllers. They didn’t give me money for telecom. They didn’t give me money for new software,” Duffy said.

“I’m coming back to Congress and the American people to explain all the great work we’re doing right now,” he continued. “We’re going to spend that $12.5 billion by the end of 2028, but I need the rest of the money for software and a new telecom architecture that will be way more resilient. I need that money so I can start that build.”

House Appropriations Committee Democrats on Sunday accused the Trump administration of freezing approximately $5.3 billion in FAA modernization funding until October 2027. Both the Office of Management and Budget and the Department of Transportation strongly dispute the claim.

In a timeline released Sunday, committee Democrats alleged OMB Director Russell Vought froze the previously approved FAA modernization funding Sept. 28. In response to an NBC News inquiry, Democrats provided an OMB apportionment document showing approximately $5.29 billion designated for fiscal year 2028, which begins Oct. 1, 2027.
While the OMB document confirms that approximately $5.29 billion is designated for fiscal year 2028 rather than fiscal year 2027, the administration disputes that the allocation constitutes a freeze.

On Saturday, NBC News reported that on Thursday, just one day before the ground stop, Duffy and Vought sent a letter to members of Congress asking lawmakers for $30.1 billion to upgrade the United States’ aging airports and air traffic control system.

They wrote: “This investment is critical to complete the modernization of our national airspace — delivering a resilient telecommunications backbone for air traffic controllers, modern hardware and software, state-of-the-art control towers, and world-class airport infrastructure. These investments will address current challenges, including weather-related delays, while preparing the National Airspace System for emerging demands, such as safely integrating air traffic with the growing space industry.”
On Sunday, Duffy urged Congress to “just do it.”

“I’m doing all I can to keep people safe,” he said. “But I’m also telling you, if you don’t give us the resources, we can’t complete the job. And this is — of all the partisanship — this is the most bipartisan thing in all of Washington. Democrats, Republicans, the president, everyone agrees on this. Let’s just do it.”

In a statement Sunday in response to questions about how the president plans to urge Congress to appropriate funds for the air traffic control infrastructure, White House spokesperson Allison Schuster said, “The Trump administration immediately stepped into action at the first sign of issue to ensure the safety and security of all Americans. President Trump put the right leadership into place to effectively handle moments like these, and yesterday, all relevant leaders came together to coordinate a plan that put the safety of the American people first.”
She added, “This administration will continue to monitor this situation and communicate to the American people through every necessary means.”

title: Evacuation lifted after suspicious device found at an ethanol plant in Peoria, Illinois
summary: A suspicious device at an ethanol plant in Peoria, Illinois, triggered a temporary evacuation request for those within a 1-mile radius, with events cancelled Friday.
story: A suspicious device at an ethanol plant in Peoria, Illinois, triggered a temporary evacuation request for those within a 1-mile radius, with events cancelled Friday.
An evacuation recommendation for those within that 1-mile radius after Friday afternoon’s discovery at the BioUrja Renewables facility was lifted Saturday, according to Peoria police.
Police and federal authorities said early Saturday that they had found a device deemed a “credible threat” and rendered it safe, without giving details as to its nature.
A search by federal, state and local authorities turned up no other devices, but an investigation into Friday’s discovery was ongoing, police said in a statement on Saturday.
“We will work tirelessly to identify the individual responsible and bring them to justice,” FBI Special Agent Ryan Presley said separately.
Peoria Mayor Rita Ali told NBC affiliate WEEK there was an “all hands on deck” response, saying: “A device has been identified. We know it’s a credible threat. We know it’s a bomb.”
​Presley told media that FBI personnel, along with local and state police, had determined a “suspicious package was a threat and rendered it safe.”
For Subscribers
Rep. Eric Sorensen, D-Ill., met with evacuees at Peoria Manual High School on Friday night.

“This is the designated shelter area for those that are impacted by the evacuation that’s going on just south of downtown Peoria,” he said in an update. “What we do need to make sure is that everybody’s making good decisions.
Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker had urged locals to “follow directions from law enforcement and stay clear of the area.”
For Subscribers
Country music singer Jon Pardi was forced to cancel his show scheduled for Friday evening at the Peoria Civic Center.
“At the direction of the Chief of Police, tonight’s concert has been canceled due to an active local safety concern,” he posted on Instagram, adding that tickets would be refunded.
The weekend’s Illinois Comic Con at Peoria Civic Center canceled its Saturday events but said after the evacuation all-clear was issued that its Sunday plans were still scheduled.
Peoria’s Caterpillar Visitors Center, Riverfront Museum, Rhythm Kitchen Music Cafe, and Main Library and Lincoln Branch library were also closed on Saturday, those venues each said on Facebook.
Dozer Park, home of the minor league baseball team the Peoria Chiefs, also canceled a holiday event at the venue.

The nearby OSF HealthCare St. Francis Medical Center said it was “taking all appropriate precautions in response to the situation in downtown Peoria.” A statement said: “We will continue to monitor the situation and take any additional steps necessary to maintain a safe environment for those we serve and those who work at our facilities.”

In 2021, Houston-based BioUrja, which has described itself as an energy, agricultural and metals commodity trading company, purchased the former ADM (Archer-Daniels-Midland) ethanol production complex in Peoria. BioUrja CEO Amit Bhandari said at the time the facility would help it expand its presence in beverage-grade and highly-distilled industrial alcohol markets.
The company did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

title: 2 injured after taxiing planes collide at Miami International Airport
summary: Two taxiing planes collided at Miami International Airport on Saturday night, officials said, a day after a nationwide ground stop disrupted flights across the country.
story: Two taxiing planes collided at Miami International Airport on Saturday night, officials said, a day after a nationwide ground stop disrupted flights across the country.

At about 9 p.m. ET Saturday, the wing tip of a Copa Airlines Boeing 737 struck the nose of a UPS Boeing 767 as both aircraft were taxiing, according to a statement from the Federal Aviation Administration.

The Copa plane was taxiing to the gate, while the UPS plane was departing for Bogota, Colombia, the FAA said. The Copa flight had six crew members and 166 passengers aboard at the time of the collision, according to a statement from the airline.
Greg Chin, a spokesperson for the Miami-Dade Aviation Department, said in a statement that two people were treated at the scene for minor injuries and were not hospitalized.
The FAA said air traffic controllers had told the UPS crew to give way to the Copa flight.

UPS said in a statement that it was aware of the incident and “committed to working with authorities to determine what happened.” “The safety of our employees and the public is our highest priority,” the company said.
For Subscribers

The collision came a day after the FAA issued a rare nationwide ground stop because of a widespread air traffic control telecommunications issue. The ground stop lasted more than four hours and led to thousands of flight cancellations and delays. Officials believe a router problem during routine work was the cause of the outage.
For Subscribers
As of 10:20 a.m. ET Sunday, 1,583 flights within, into or out of the U.S. had been canceled, and another 2,944 were delayed.
Last year, 15 people were killed when a UPS cargo plane crashed just outside of Louisville, Kentucky’s Louisville Muhammad Ali International Airport.

title: Trump plans to take Qatari jet to Asia, but it’s unclear whether it’s been ‘maxed out’
summary: President Donald Trump is expected to take the Qatari-gifted Air Force One to Asia on Monday as questions linger about upgrades the White House said were needed after a security threat from Iran forced the president to fly home from Turkey on a secret military plane in July, according to two U.S. officials.
story: President Donald Trump is expected to take the Qatari-gifted Air Force One to Asia on Monday as questions linger about upgrades the White House said were needed after a security threat from Iran forced the president to fly home from Turkey on a secret military plane in July, according to two U.S. officials.

For months, Trump has said the jet from the Qataris would be “going away” to get “maxed out” so it could “go into any territory.” In September, he said those changes to the plane would “take about 60 days.” The president flew on the new Air Force One to Ireland that month without any issues. He then used the plane regularly during a midterm travel blitz in October, which meant it was not out of commission for an extended period.

Instead, the plane has received some improvements and periodic maintenance, but it is unclear whether it has been fully “maxed out,” per the officials. A longer upgrade period is expected in the future, according to one of the officials, but those upgrades will not take a full 60 days.
For Subscribers

In recent months, the plane has received some “cosmetic” enhancements to the interior, the other U.S. official said, but that did not cover the larger work that the White House said would take place eventually.

“We don’t comment on specific upgrades or modifications to Air Force Once,” a senior administration official told NBC News in a statement. “We maintain a consistent posture that ensures a safe, secure, and reliable capability for the President of the United States and routinely evolve the capability as required to maintain that posture. It is the greatest Presidential plane ever built.”
For Subscribers
In July, Trump said the plane “has a lot of capability.”

“But as I understand it, in about a month ​or so, they’re gonna send it to have it be maxed out,” he said. “It’ll take about a month.” Trump did not detail the nature of the work, and the White House has not explained why the original assessment of 30 days later doubled to 60 days.

At the time, then-White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt said in a statement that the new Air Force One was “perfectly safe” for domestic and overseas travel but noted in July that the plane would “receive additional upgrades and enhancements in the fall which will take approximately one month to complete.”

title: Why Mary Peltola is on track to win in Alaska, even if ranked choice ballots come into play
summary: As Alaska continues to count and report votes weeks after Election Day, it is increasingly unlikely that Republican Sen.
story: As Alaska continues to count and report votes weeks after Election Day, it is increasingly unlikely that Republican Sen. Dan S. Sullivan will hang on to his job.

His Democratic challenger, Mary Peltola, is on track to win the still-unresolved Senate race under either possible scenario — with an outright majority, or if the race goes to ranked choice ballots, according to an NBC News Decision Desk analysis of outstanding and tabulated votes.

Peltola currently leads Sullivan by 3.7 percentage points, or just over 10,000 votes. With 96% of the expected vote in, NBC News’ Decision Desk now believes Peltola is likely to win this race, though we may need to wait until Wednesday, Nov. 18, to know the final result.

If no candidate receives over 50% of the vote, Alaska determines a winner using ranked choice voting, in which the lowest-ranked candidates are eliminated one by one and their votes are redistributed according to each voter’s ranked preferences. If a voter did not rank the remaining candidates, their ballots are considered “exhausted” and are excluded from the final vote count.

Wednesday is Alaska’s deadline for final mail absentee ballots to be received by election officials, one reason why this close race has lingered for so long. Alaska reports its votes unevenly, and NBC News expects to see the remainder of these votes early next week.
Nov. 18 is also the day the state Division of Elections would run the ranked choice tabulation, if needed.

If Peltola receives over 50% of the vote, she will win the election without needing to go through the ranked choice tabulation process. She needs to win just 53.8% of the remaining ballots to clear this mark — a real possibility given her strength in recent vote reports. On Friday night, she received 58% of the newly reported votes.

Sullivan, the incumbent, has two separate paths to gain ground and win the election: making up the gap with first-choice rankings, or making up the gap via the ranked choice process. An NBC News Decision Desk analysis of the ballots already tabulated shows that the first route is highly improbable and that the second route is likely impossible.

The first route that Sullivan could use to come back would be passing Peltola in first-choice rankings. With approximately 12,000 votes outstanding, Sullivan would need to win around 92%  of those in order to tie with Peltola. That would amount to about 46 points better than he has performed in the vote counted so far, and far above the percentage either candidate has achieved in any batch of ballots received up to this point. On Friday night, he received just 38% of newly reported votes.
The second route for Sullivan to retake the lead is through the ranked choice process, but an analysis of the ballots shows why this route is effectively closed to him.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

There are currently 11,300 tallied ballots with first-choice votes for candidates other than Peltola and Sullivan. Those ballots may be redistributed in the ranked choice process. With 4% of the total vote outstanding, the number of ballots with first-choice votes for candidates other than Peltola and Sullivan could rise to around 12,000. For Sullivan to net 10,400 ballots out of a pool of 12,000 and close the gap with Peltola, he would need to win around 93% of redistributed votes.
However, even that steep figure is misleadingly optimistic for Sullivan because of what we already know about how people are ranking the candidates.
The Alaska Division of Elections posts a “Cast Vote Record” for the over-270,000 ballots currently tabulated. These records show exactly how each candidate is ranked on each ballot.

Our analysis of those ballots shows that Sullivan does gain some votes from the ranked choice process, receiving a large transfer of votes from voters who backed Republican Gerald Heikes, who is in third place. But the most important thing about these votes is that a large percentage of ballots from those who backed other candidates are “exhausted” in the ranked choice tabulation process.

Over 45% of voters who ranked Heikes, Dan J. Sullivan Jr. or a write-in candidate did not rank Peltola or Sen. Dan S. Sullivan as a later choice, which means that these ballots will play no role in the ranked choice tabulation.
This ballot exhaustion means that there are far fewer than 12,000 ballots available for Sullivan to make up the gap of about 10,000 votes between him and Peltola in the ranked choice process.

If current rates are maintained, only about 6,600 ballots will actually be redistributed to the top two finishers in the ranked choice tabulation. If Sullivan is more than 6,600 votes behind Peltola’s first-choice margin after all ballots have been counted, it is mathematically impossible for the Republican incumbent to catch up to Peltola in the ranked choice tabulation.

The NBC News Decision Desk will need to assess the remaining ballots as they are received to determine if our standards are met to officially project the race, or whether the outcome will be determined by the ranked choice process carried out by the Alaska Division of Elections.

title: Michael J. Fox, Tracy Pollan and All 3 Daughters Stun in Rare Red Carpet Appearance Together
summary: Michael J. Fox posed with wife and fellow actor Tracy Pollan, along with all three of their daughters, Esmé Annabelle Fox, 25, and twins Schuyler Fox and Aquinnah Kathleen Fox, 31, in a rare appearance together at his annual gala.
story: It’s a family affair!
Actor Michael J. Fox hit the red carpet on Nov. 14 with his family for his foundation’s annual gala, “A Funny Thing Happened On The Way To Cure Parkinson’s” event in New York City.

The 65-year-old posed with wife and fellow actor Tracy Pollan, along with all three of their daughters, Esmé Annabelle Fox, 25, and twins Schuyler Fox and Aquinnah Kathleen Fox, 31, in a rare appearance all together. The couple’s son, Sam Michael Fox, was not in attendance.

Michael J. Fox, who founded the Michael J. Fox Foundation for Parkinson’s Research in 2000, sported a T-shirt under a more formal jacket. Meanwhile, Pollan and the couple’s daughters rocked stunning gowns for the event.

The night was a particularly eventful one, as it not only featured star-studded attendees from Stephen Colbert and David Letterman to TODAY’s Willie Geist, but also several comedy and musical performances.
Among those to take the stage were John Mayer, Brad Paisley and Michael J. Fox himself, who rocked out on the electric guitar.
Comedians, including Josh Johnson and Tom Papa, also performed sets throughout the night.

Fox has been a vocal proponent of Parkinson’s research. In September, he was awarded the Bob Hope Humanitarian Award at the Emmys for his philanthropy. In his acceptance speech, Fox offered some hopeful remarks.
“I’m proud of the progress we’ve made to benefit Parkinsons patients, and families,” Fox said in his acceptance speech. “We move closer to eradicating this disease forever.”
Fox, who was diagnosed in 1991, kept the information private for years before opening up about the disease until 1998.
During a 2020 interview with Willie, Fox discussed his journey to accepting the diagnosis.

“You eventually come to a place where you go, ‘I can do this.’ This is just the way it is. It’s something that happened to me. It’s not something I’m suffering from. It’s my reality,” he said. “I find that the partner of gratitude is acceptance and surrender.”

title: Snooki Gifts Internet With ‘The Poof’ Tutorial As the 2000s Hairstyle Makes a Comeback
summary: If there’s one person we can learn from in creating the most authentic 2000s hair poof, it’s the “Jersey Shore” queen herself, Snooki.
story: If there’s one person we can learn from in creating the most authentic 2000s hair poof, it’s the “Jersey Shore” queen herself, Snooki.
Snooki, whose real name is Nicole Polizzi, took to social media to share a tutorial for the iconic hairstyle that she so famously rocked on the MTV reality show.
The video, posted Nov. 14, comes as the millennial hair trend has been revived by younger generations across social media. And Snooki just had to show the youth how it’s done.
“I’ve been summoned by a lot of you talking about a trend that might be coming back — a hair trend, if you will — from the younger generation,” Snooki says in the video.
She adds: “We’re talking about ‘the poof.’”
And fans were unsurprisingly delighted by the tutorial from the Queen of Poofs.
“it’s like watching the Mona Lisa being painted,” a TikTok user wrote.
Another person wrote on TikTok that “Snooki wearing a poof in 2026 has healed something in me 🥰😭🖤”

Snooki, who rose to fame after the premiere of the reality show in the 2009, became known for her peak millennial look that often involved a tan, graphic tanks, heavy black eyeliner, animal prints and, of course, the signature Poof. So, she certainly has the credentials to teach us all a thing or two.

In the video, Snooki starts off, clarifying that the hairstyle should be referred as “The Poof,” rather than “the hair bump.” She also expresses a strong distaste for the “Bumpit,” the iconic hair tool that many millennials used to create the voluminous style. The reality star then explains some other common faux pas that she’s noticed.

“They’re showing themselves doing the hair bump with bobby pins. Bobby pins. Bobby pins! I don’t know what’s happening. What are we doing?” she says in the video. “So I feel like the mother hen needs to come in and say, “Girls, no, no. If we’re gonna bring this back and do it, do it the right way. We have to do it the right way.”
Snooki then dives into her step-by-step instructions to re-create the look. It goes a little something like this:
Tease the Section of Hair That You Plan To Use for the Poof
“For me, I always had thick hair. I never really needed to tease, but obviously, if you got a tease, you tease the s--- out of it,” Snooki says.
This part, she underscores is not to be taken lightly.
“You do it for a long time. OK? A long time,” she says of the teasing.
Grab a Clip — Not a Bobby Pin
After the section of hair is properly teased, gather the section with a hair clip.
“These clips, you get it from Sally’s. They’re 99 cents,” Snooki says. “This is the clip you use. No bobby pins.”
Secure the poof onto your head with the clip.
Hairspray, Duh!
Next comes an essential aspect of the hairstyle: Hairspray.
In the tutorial, Snooki applies hairspray extremely liberally to the poofed section of hair.
Finish It Off by Fanning out the Poof
Fan out the poof so that the strands form a perfect rainbow shape.
“Make it nice and cute, and you can even go bigger,” Snooki says, as she arranges her strands. “I used to go way bigger.”
And there you have it!

title: John Mulaney Sells You an Age-Old Parental Care System, ‘Sister,’ in ‘SNL’ Skit That’s Too Real
summary: Comedian John Mulaney, who hosted the Nov. 14 episode of “Saturday Night Live,” portrayed a salesman who’s promoting a convenient elder care system known as “Sister.” And for many families, this one’s a little too real.
story: This one goes out to all the devoted daughters out there!

Comedian John Mulaney, who hosted the Nov. 14 episode of “Saturday Night Live,” portrayed a salesman who’s promoting a convenient elder care system known as “Sister.” And for many families, this one’s a little too real.
In the “ad,” Mulaney begins by presenting the quintessential dilemma for people who don’t want to turn to outside help to care for aging parents.

“My dad means the world to me. So when I noticed him start to slow down, I knew I needed to get him the best care possible,” he says. “I didn’t want to put him in a nursing home, but a private health aide could cost thousands a week. I didn’t know where to turn. That’s when I heard about ‘Sister.’”
“Sister,” Mulaney explains, is a free, 24/7 elder care provider who is “also your sister.”

“Now I don’t have to worry about Dad getting the care and attention he needs because my sister will do it, and I can get back to my life and the stuff I like to do,” he says. His sister, who is portrayed by Jane Wickline, scrambles to make sure their dad is cared for.
The sketch also features some of the show’s male cast members, raving about the elder care system.
“I love my mom more than anything. That doesn’t mean I want to help her in the bathroom. Sister doesn’t either, but she will. Whereas I won’t,” Andrew Dismukes says. “That’s the sister difference.”
Mikey Day — who plays character Dr. Grant, author of “Not It! A Son’s Guide To Elder Care” — breaks down the system for viewers.

“Here’s how it works. First, years of internalized sexism warps sister’s brain into thinking caretaking is her responsibility and somehow not yours,” Dr. Grant says. “Next, your text arrives, instantly activating her, and that’s it. You’re done for life. See you at the funeral!”
Mulaney concludes the commercial by offering an extra special offer.
“Sign up now, and we’ll throw in sister’s husband, whether he likes it or not,” he says.
Oof.
For many viewers, the dark humor sketch was just way too honest.
“I was Sister. This sketch was too accurate,” one person wrote in the comments on YouTube.
Another person wrote that they were “laughing so hard because this hit WAY too close to home!”
“SNL, I did NOT give you permission to turn my family drama into a skit!” the social media user said.

The Nov. 14 show marked Mulaney’s seventh time hosting. The former “SNL” writer’s big night was well-received and included several major highlights like former cast member Bowen Yang’s return to the Studio 8H stage.

title: Bowen Yang Makes Electric Return to ‘SNL’ As Ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen ‘Hide Your Wife’ Huang
summary: Bowen Yang surprised audiences on Nov. 14 with an electrifying appearance on the latest episode of “Saturday Night Live.” Yang, who departed the sketch comedy show in 2025, returned during the cold open to play disgraced ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.
story: He’s back like he never left!

Former cast member Bowen Yang surprised audiences on Nov. 14 with an electrifying appearance on the latest episode of “Saturday Night Live.” Yang, who departed the sketch comedy show in 2025, returned during the cold open to play disgraced ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.
Yang, sporting gray hair and a leather jacket, performed a hilarious spoof of the tech billionaire.
“It’s me, Jensen ‘Hide Your Wife’ Huang,” Yang says. “Ladies, when you invite Jensen over, you know what’s about to go down — the S&P 500.”

In the skit, host John Mulaney plays a CIA official who gathers the nation’s most prominent tech billionaires, from Elon Musk to Sam Altman, for a training on how to distinguish between a spy and a woman who’s actually interested in them.
Mulaney, referencing Huang’s scandal, asks the group, “What do you think the lesson is here?”
Facebook founder Mark Zuckerberg, played by cast member Andrew Dismukes, responds, “Never date a human woman.”
Mulaney really attempts to get his point across, at one point resorting to some visual aids.

“Now I know you dorks like charts, so let’s take a look at this Venn diagram,” Mulaney says while pointing to a graphic on a screen. “On this side we have beautiful women, and on this side we have people who would be interested in your shared opinions and interests. I cannot stress this enough. There is no overlap.”
As Mulaney attempts to inform the clueless tech bosses, with little avail, he decides to pivot to a different strategy.
“Maybe what would help is if I hand it over to someone who learned this lesson the hard way,” Mulaney says, before Yang walks into the room.
“Fellas, don’t be like me,” “Jensen” says, delivering his cautionary tale. “Remember, women don’t like guys like us. That’s how we became guys like us.”

The cold open isn’t the only appearance Yang made in the show. He also made another cameo as Mary Todd Lincoln in “Little Park of Horrors,” a musical sketch in which Mulaney plays a sad horse carriage operator who’s lamenting the recent horse-drawn carriage ban in New York City.

Yang, who is currently playing Mary Todd Lincoln in the hit Broadway play “Oh, Mary!,” steps in to sing a parody of “And I’m Telling You I’m Not Going” from “Dreamgirls” about a ride through the Lincoln Tunnel.

Yang left “SNL” midway through his eight season on the show. During his time on the sketch comedy show, Yang became a major breakout star, with some of his most memorable roles being his impression of viral pygmy hippo Moo Deng and the iceberg that sank the Titanic.

title: ‘Love Is Blind’ Season 11 Star Rob Feeley Unpacks ‘Tough to Watch’ Moments and Where He and Michaella Stand Now
summary: Rob Feeley is ready to unpack his tumultuous season of “Love Is Blind.” He opens up to TODAY.com about his relationship with Michaella Giorgio.
story: Rob Feeley is ready to unpack his tumultuous season of “Love Is Blind.”

The 40 year old, who works in AI infrastructure sales, was highlighted early on in Season 11 of the Netflix dating show for his rowdy personality. His demeanor was one of the many reasons Michaella Giorgio fell for him in the pods. The two got engaged and developed a stronger connection during their couples’ trip to Mexico.

Back in Boston, they met each other’s families and seemed poised to become a “Love Is Blind” success story. But their relationship took a drastic turn when Giorgio was introduced to Feeley’s friends, with some fans calling out Feeley and the men for how they treated Giorgio during the interaction. The next day, Feeley spiraled at a cast meetup and he and Michaella later broke up.
“I think looking back, 100% I should have stepped in and hindsight’s 20/20,” he tells TODAY.com after watching the awkward exchange between his friend group and Giorgio.
He adds that he and the one particular friend who rubbed some viewers the wrong way “had a serious conversation after watching that whole thing.”
“It was not a good situation. It was really tough to watch,” he shares.

Below, he opens up more about the unraveling of his relationship with Giorgio, including conversations the two had after they exited the experiment. He also reveals details about the lifestyle changes he made following the show and why he adjusted his stance on therapy.
This interview has been edited and condensed for clarity.
I mean, some ups and some downs. But overall, it’s been OK.

I think looking back, 100% I should have stepped in. Hindsight’s 20/20. But looking at it on camera, which I didn’t have the opportunity, there were a lot of situations that I wish I could have taken back, and especially my friend. My friend and I had a serious conversation after watching that whole thing. It was not a good situation. It was really tough to watch.

If there’s anyone that is embarrassed about that whole situation, it’s my friend. He was not in a good place post that conversation, in regards to seeing it back. Obviously, I think we can all agree he was a little bit intoxicated. It’s not a secret, and I think that if there’s anyone who is regretful and really, really sad about that situation, it’s him. He’s very, very apologetic to Michaella and the whole situation, and if he could take it back, he would every second of the day.

I can’t control the questions my friends ask. I think my friends protect me just like anyone’s friends. So I think that we just wanted to make sure that everyone’s there for the right reasons. I don’t think there was any malintent in asking those questions. I asked Morrey Eglin that question actually. I’m like, “What are you here for?” There was no agenda behind that. I think that everyone just kind of is wondering, like, “What’s going on? Who’s here for the right intentions?” But that’s not indicative to who Michaella is. I don’t think she was here for the wrong intentions, obviously. You can clearly see post-show she’s not here for the wrong intentions.
I’m not really sure. I think I just wanted to trust the process, and I feel like I just want to keep going through the process.

I can’t really recall in terms of that. Diana and I had a great relationship in the pods. She’s awesome. She’s amazing. I don’t really know. I don’t really recall in regards to, like, the canceling thing. I said it a few times. I don’t really know to be honest.

I didn’t really have many concerns. I think I just was there to just find my person, and at the end of the day, I wish I did and unfortunately I didn’t. I didn’t really have a ton of concerns. You know, it’s “Love Is Blind,” and I’d never watched the show in my entire life. I went on legit to find love.

Because I was 38 years old at the time, I wanted to find my person, and I felt like it was a very cool way to find your person, and not just have to look at the exterior. Have that person’s soul, that person’s heart, that person’s personality mean more to you than what they look like on the outside.

My friends were, like, because they obviously knew I was looking for love. I was in my late 30s. They’re just like, “Hey, I think this’d be a good idea because you’re at that position in your life where you’re looking for your forever person. You’re going to take it very seriously. Like, you’re not someone who’s going to go on here to not take it seriously.” They’re like, “Throw your name in the hat.”
I just think I was overwhelmed overall. I think Michaela deserved way better. So at that time, I was like, “You know what, you deserve better.” That’s pretty much it.

I think there wasn’t really an overall like one-on-one, we’re going to end it now. I think that at that moment at Lansdowne (Pub), I guess she ended it. Then I went for my exit interview, and I was informed that she ended it. So, yeah, that was kind of it.
I think everyone was hurt.

No, so we talked right after my exit interview. We spoke. We hung out post the breakup, and then we just would (stay) in touch. Then eventually, she’s like, “Hey, Rob, I don’t think I can stay in communication anymore. You know, it’s not easy for me.” I said, “OK, no problem,” and that was it. So I respect a person’s boundaries. I wanted to stay cordial, but she said, “Hey, it’s not easy for me to just talk to you and be your friend.” I said, “OK, no worries. I respect your decision.”

Not too sure. We were supposed to be season 10, and then I think I reached out. We had a lot of conversations. I think I reached out. I was like, “Hey, how do you feel about this?” And then she’s like, “Hey, it’s not easy for me to speak to you and I need to move on.” I said, “No problem.” That was it.

Of course. It wasn’t just 50 days. It was 75 after that. It’s my whole lifestyle. But I felt like I needed to take a moment to myself, or 50 days to myself, and just reflect, work on myself. Anyone that knows me knows this. It was a very intense experience for me, and I did not do this for the clout. I was just working on myself and being by myself for a lot of that time … being with my family, my close friends, and I didn’t really want to be in the outside world.

I think that I just looked at it in a different perspective. I was like, “You know what? Maybe this can work.” Because I had been to therapy, like when I was young. So I just think that I needed to talk to somebody about my whole experience. Not just my experience on “Love Is Blind,” but just in life.

I would say that maybe it was a little bit of an eye opener. But again, you don’t know my life, and a lot of people don’t. But those 15 days were very tough in regards to, like, I don’t want to ever hurt somebody. What I’ve been through, and things in my past, like, that’s why on the show I didn’t really dive into it because I made a promise to myself and my family I wasn’t going to dive into certain things that (are) personal. So I didn’t want to dive into all those things if that makes sense. But I did think after the show in certain moments, I had to reflect. I’m like, “S---. I should probably talk to somebody.”
I think, again, for me, it was just the pressure. It was a lot, and I feel like you know when you hurt somebody, it’s not easy to come back. So, yeah, I think his assessment was fairly right.

I would say I learned a lot about myself, and if I could do things differently, I would have. And don’t let the emotion get the best of you. I probably should have communicated better early in the process.

title: Lucille Ball Reminisces About ‘I Love Lucy’ In 1983 TODAY Interview
summary: Lucille Ball talked to TODAY in 1983 about what it took to create “I Love Lucy” and how she overcame obstacles to do so.
story: As TODAY marks its 75th anniversary, the TODAY Archive is revisiting legendary interviews, stories that moved us and other iconic moments from our 75 years on the air. These are the segments that shaped TODAY and created a lasting legacy. Today, we look back at Lucille Ball talking about the legacy of “I Love Lucy” on Feb. 16, 1983.
“I Love Lucy” was an American institution when star Lucille Ball sat down with Jane Pauley to look back at the pioneering sitcom on Feb. 16, 1983.

“I Love Lucy” premiered Oct. 15, 1951 — nearly three months to the day before TODAY would first sign on — and ran for six seasons, living on for decades beyond that in syndication. It chronicled a middle-class wife (Ball), who often gets involved in hairbrained schemes, much to the chagrin of her husband, played by Ball’s real-life husband, Desi Arnaz.
As Ball, who died in 1989, told Pauley, though, the show almost never got off the ground.
Did Lucille Ball Think She Was a Trailblazer?
“I Love Lucy” remains one of the most beloved shows ever, but Ball didn’t consider the idea that she was some sort of visionary.
“No ... I was only going to work for about a year, a year or two, so that I had something like home movies to show my baby. I was pregnant at the time,” she said.
Her daughter, Lucie, was born in 1951, and her son, Desi Jr., would be born in 1953, with the pregnancy famously being written into the show.
CBS wanted Ball and her husband to come up with an idea for a show. However, the network didn’t want him involved, also insisting the show shoot in New York.

“I stuck to my guns,” Ball said. “I said, ‘I certainly don’t want to quit pictures and do television and have to move to New York. That doesn’t make sense. I want to stay home and have babies, and that’s why we want to work together.’ And they said, ‘Well, it didn’t seem quite right to have a Cuban husband for a young American couple.’ I said, ‘Why not? We are married.’ Well, they still didn’t buy it.”
“You gotta admit, it does sound like an odd pairing, doesn’t it?” Pauley asked.
“And it was,” Ball shot back, with a laugh.
Ball and Arnaz had no interest in shooting in New York. So when CBS threatened to drop the show, Ball said she and Arnaz “scraped together $5,000” which helped them gain ownership of it.
How About Those Co-Stars?!
“I Love Lucy” was enhanced by the presence of Vivian Vance and William Frawley, who played married couple Ethel and Fred Mertz, respectively.
“We had an idea of what we wanted and they were available. They were there at the right time, the right place, and thank God we found them,” Ball said.
“It was a very, very close, well-knit marriage of two married generations, the older marrieds and the younger marrieds,” she said, “and that was what made it so marvelous to play the satire against.”
How Did Lucille Ball Approach the Show?

Calling herself a connoisseur of the show, Pauley admitted she could probably do some routines from it. This prompted Ball to ask if she could “Vitameatavegamin,” a reference to the famous episode where Lucy gets a job in a commercial for a tonic that, unbeknownst to her, has a lot of alcohol in it.
Pauley then tried to pronounce Vitameatavegamin, with help from Ball.
Before their sit down ended, the comedy icon reflected on audience reception to her show.

“A lot of people don’t love Lucy, especially when they’re working, they don’t think of it that way,” she said, before stressing the grueling schedule. “But I had a show to get on, and we had our timing down a certain way.

“We had to accomplish a lot of things by a certain time, and if I hadn’t accomplished them, I knew that I was way behind,” she explained, “because we did our show from 10 o’clock Monday morning and we did it in front of an audience at 3 o’clock Thursday afternoon.”
She added, “And every minute counted.”

title: Jenna Dewan Addresses Shocking ‘DWTS’ Exit, Partner Val Chmerkovskiy’s Brief Suspension
summary: Actor Jenna Dewan just opened up in a recent interview about her elimination from “Dancing With the Stars,” after weeks dominating the reality competition show’s leaderboard.
story: Actor Jenna Dewan just opened up in a recent interview about her elimination from “Dancing With the Stars,” after weeks dominating the reality competition show’s leaderboard.

Dewan, who exited the show after the latest Grammy Night-themed episode, spoke to Women’s Health about her run on the competition, the mid-season controversy involving her dance partner, pro Val Chmerkovskiy, and her departure. She told the outlet that she’s feeling “all kinds of things” but is “mostly proud.”

“I feel really proud of myself, and I feel proud of the last dance we gave on the ballroom floor, and I feel obviously sad that it’s over, that I don’t get to give any more dances out there and create any more special pieces,” Dewan told the outlet. “So I think it’s really both. I feel really proud of us, and I feel fulfilled, and I feel filled up, and I also feel sad that the journey of creating dances is over.”
Dewan called the journey an “enormous undertaking, and it’s  physically, emotionally, mentally, spiritually intense.”
“And so, when that’s just finished, it’s like a light switch goes off, and then you almost don’t even know where you are,” she said.

Dewan and Chmerkovskiy competed together on the show for nine weeks. Dewan, who has a dance background, proved to be a strong contender for the Mirrorball Trophy, often receiving high scores for routines that have ranged from jazz to quickstep.

However the pair’s run was interrupted when Chmerkovskiy was handed a one-week suspension, the show announced Oct. 17, due to a status he posted on TikTok that appeared to reference Will Smith’s notorious altercation with Chris Rock at the 2022 Oscars. The pro had been reacting to the harsh critique that judge Carrie Ann Inaba gave his wife, fellow pro Jenna Johnson who’s paired up with actor Harry Shum Jr.
As a result, Chmerkovskiy missed the show’s signature Dedication Night. And Dewan was instead paired up with pro Alan Bersten for that week.
Chmerkovskiy has since apologized for the incident.

“I made a poor decision to reference a meme to ‘keep my wife’s name’ out of the conversation, without stopping to think through what else that reference could imply, which was genuinely never my intention,” he wrote in his Instagram story, referencing Smith’s words to Rock amid the Oscars spat, “Keep my wife’s name out of your f------ mouth.”
Dewan told Women’s Health that she “did not foresee having as many challenges as I did that were thrown at me during my Dancing with the Stars journey.”

“However, the challenges of it gave me an opportunity to walk my talk, and I always think that when that happens, you can go back to your true north, to what’s your intention for doing something,” she told the outlet. “How do you want to show up as a human when you’re experiencing challenges? And I kept going back to my kids.”
She added that when the mid-season suspension went down, she chose to take the high road.
“I thought, ‘I have a real opportunity here. I can be annoyed and bitter and upset about this, or I can show up with grace and love and joy and focus on the moment,’” she told Women’s Health.
Dewan also said that she was intent on keeping her attention on her family. After all, that week’s Dedication Night dance was an ode to her mother.

“She was in town, thrilled to have this dance with me, and thrilled to experience this moment. And I thought that this is something she’s going to remember,” Dewan said. “We’re all going to remember my family forever. Let’s focus on that, and let’s not worry about all of this that’s going on.”
As the rest of the season shakes out, the actor shared a few more thoughts in an Instagram post Nov. 14. In it, she reflected on returning to dance, a craft that she’s long enjoyed.

“There’s something beautiful about returning to what you love, not as the person you once were, but as everything you’ve become,” Dewan wrote. “To everyone who showed up for us, voted, cheered and sent love… thank you!!! I felt it all ❤️”
She also had some lovely words for Chmerkovskiy.
“To Val- to learn from one of the best to ever do it is a gift I’ll treasure forever!” she wrote. “Thank you for your passion, creativity and friendship throughout this entire crazy ride🙏🏻”

title: Tyriq Withers, Daniel Kaluuya Go Viral For Hilariously Chaotic Local News Interview Amid FAA Ground Stop
summary: Tyriq Withers and Daniel Kaluuya, who were scheduled to be on a flight to Los Angeles, joined local television station KVAL in Eugene, Oregon, to share their take on the situation.
story: While the nationwide ground stop threw travelers across the country into chaos Nov. 13, actors Tyriq Withers and Daniel Kaluuya certainly made the most of their interrupted plans.
The two, who were scheduled to be on a flight to Los Angeles, joined local television station KVAL in Eugene, Oregon, to share their take on the situation.
While the interview started out quite ordinarily, with Withers speaking about how he and Kaluuya were forced to deboard amid the news, things quickly took a hilarious turn.
“It’s really upsetting me and my home girl because if you can’t go to the airport, where the hell can you go?” Withers told KVAL, before his “home girl” Kaluuya dissolved into giggles.

The “Him” actor, of course, referenced the viral Bella Noche nightclub meme from a 2015 news segment in which a partygoer, identified as Hazel London, reacted to a violence at the Baton Rouge nightclub with the now-famous phrase, “Well damn. If you can’t go to Bella Noche’s then where the hell can you go?!”

The Federal Aviation Administration halted departures for more than four hours due to what the agency said was “due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety.” Later on, officials said that ground stop was due to an equipment outage that disrupted radar feeds and communications with aircraft.The FAA lifted the ground stop at 8:15 p.m. ET.
During the interview with KVAL, Kaluuya kept things light, sharing that he was “grateful” that they were safe.

“I feel grateful. Obviously, it’s an inconvenience, but I feel grateful,” Kaluuya told the outlet. “I feel grateful because it could have happened any other way. Think about how many lives we probably saved because of that decision.”
He and Withers ended their segment by hyping up Eugene, Oregon.
Now that’s one way to pass the time!

title: Mom of ‘Breaking Bad’ Star RJ Mitte Shares Heartbreaking Tribute 1 Month After His Death
summary: Dyna Mitte, the mother of RJ Mitte, shared a moving tribute to the late “Breaking Bad” actor on the recent one-month anniversary of his death.
story: Dyna Mitte, the mother of RJ Mitte, shared a moving tribute to the late “Breaking Bad” actor on the recent one-month anniversary of his death.
In the post shared on Instagram Nov. 13,  Dyna Mitte reflected on the weeks since RJ Mitte died by suicide. He was 34.
Written as an open letter to the late actor, Dyna Mitte said that she misses him “so much it hurts.”

“My beautiful boy, it has been a month since you left us. I miss you so much it hurts,” Dyna Mitte wrote. “There are days that it feels like it happen today, and at times it feels like forever ago. I am trying to navigate through this new life, but it is so painfully difficult.”

RJ Mitte, best known for his role as Walter “Flynn” White Jr. on “Breaking Bad,” was also a philanthropist and disability rights advocate. He died on Oct. 12 in Brownsville, Texas, where lived, the Brownsville Justice of the Peace confirmed.

Dyna Mitte previously told NBC News that actor had no history of mental illness, however he had been going through a difficult emotional time. Still, he made no indication that he might end his life, she said.
In her latest post, Dyna Mitte wrote that she wished she could “just look” at her son again.
“What I would not give to hold you again, see that beautiful smile, laugh at the crazy conversations we had, are just look at you,” she wrote. “I love you forever + time.”
Dyna Mitte concluded her post with a wish.
“Please continue to watch over us,” she wrote. “With all my love, Mom”

The tribute comes after RJ Mitte’s sister Lacianne Carriere also opened up about her struggles with her grief. In an Oct. 24 Instagram post, Carriere wrote that she had been having a difficult time, wrapping her mind around his death.

“I just really need my brother right now…You would put on some lofi music and tell me to get up and go sit in the shower, how it always makes you feel better,” she wrote. “I know you’re telling me right now that I’ll be okay though I don’t know how I will. But I promise I’m going to do my hardest and I promise your love will always live through me until the day I see you again.”

title: Beyoncé Reveals New Details Around Her ‘Very Small’ Private 2008 Wedding to Jay-Z
summary: In a recent interview with British publication i-D Magazine, Queen Bey revealed that her nuptials were a complete surprise to the couple’s wedding guests.
story: Hold up — Beyoncé just gave us a few more deets about her 2008 wedding to media mogul Jay-Z.
In a recent interview with British publication i-D Magazine, Queen Bey revealed that her nuptials were a complete surprise to the couple’s wedding guests.

“We had a very small wedding in our home,” the musician said in the interview, published Nov. 11. “We told the guests we were having a party, and no one knew they were coming to our wedding but our parents and a few friends.”

Beyoncé and Jay-Z tied the knot on April 4, 2008, with the date (4/4) being a nod to the couple’s birthdays: Beyonce was born on September 4 while Jay-Z was born on December 4. Several stars, including Beyoncé’s former Destiny’s Child bandmates, Kelly Rowland and Michelle Williams, and Gwyneth Paltrow, were spotted that day outside Jay-Z’s Tribeca home.
But little has been shared about the intimate wedding over the years.
In the interview with i-D, the singer said that her mother Tina Knowles, who had served as the stylist for Destiny’s Child’s for years, designed her wedding dress.
“My favourite dress my mother designed was my wedding dress—it was gorgeously simple and made with her love,” she told the outlet.
The “Cowboy Carter” singer told the outlet that the ensemble is one of her most cherished looks.
“Wearing a dress she designed was very important to me, and more important than any designer dress,” Beyoncé told i-D.
The artist, who’s been with Jay-Z for over two decades, shares three children with the rapper: Blue Ivy Carter, 14, and twins Rumi and Sir Carter, 9.

The couple has been famously private about their family life. Beyoncé shared a few seconds of footage from their wedding day in her 2011 live video for song “I Was Here.” Years later in 2015, Jay-Z shared a video from their big day on Instagram in a since-deleted post.

title: ‘Emo Gods’ Hoobastank, Simple Plan Surprised Fans on Plane With Mid-Air Performances
summary: While most travelers across the U.S. navigated chaos during the Federal Aviation Administration’s nationwide ground stop Nov.
story: While most travelers across the U.S. navigated chaos during the Federal Aviation Administration’s nationwide ground stop Nov. 13, some lucky flyers had a day that would make any millennial who sported emo bangs and fingerless gloves in high school proud.
Several alt rock acts, including Hoobastank and Simple Plan, showed up at a Southwest flight and performed some of their hits for those on board.

The flight, which left out of Los Angeles, had just missed the ground stop, so the bands were able to rock out for the passengers at 35,000 feet in the air, according to a press release about the event.
Fan videos posted to social media captured the performances. And when Hoobastank began playing their 2004 smash hit “The Reason” down the aisles, the crowd couldn’t help but sing.
A clip shared on the band’s official Instagram page shows the plane full of passengers, holding up their phones with the flashlight feature on, swaying to the acoustic set.
Another from the flight shows Simple Plan, performing their 2002 song “I’m Just A Kid.”
Other performers included The Used, who played their 2002 single “The Taste of Ink” and LØLØ.

According to a press release about the event, the bands showed up to a flight that was part of Southwest’s “Live at 35” music program, which features pop-up performances. This particular gig took place just ahead of the Vans Warped Tour Orlando stop this weekend at Camping World Stadium Campus.
The performances certainly brought a bit of levity to an otherwise frustrating day for travelers. People across social media couldn’t help but be just a bit jealous of those on board.
“this is the worst fomo I’ve ever had” one person wrote on social media.
Same, same.

title: Karin Slaughter Reveals the Most Important Line in ‘The Good Daughter’ and It’s a Message All Women Need to Hear
summary: Warning: This story contains spoilers for “The Good Daughter.”
story: Warning: This story contains spoilers for “The Good Daughter.”

From the moment two masked men with guns step into the home of teenage sisters Samantha and Charlotte Quinn, it’s clear that crime drama “The Good Daughter” is a story about survival — what happens after violence changes the trajectory of your life, and the pain of piecing together your past.
It’s just one of several traumatic plot points in the six-episode series, based on the book of the same name by bestselling author Karin Slaughter, out Nov. 12 on Peacock.
While sexual violence is a theme in much of Slaughter’s work, extra care was given to how this story was brought to the small screen, Slaughter tells TODAY.com.

“One of the things I’m most proud of in this show is I set these rules that we were only going to tell the story from the perspective of Sam or Charlie,” she says. “If it’s young Charlie, (director Steph Green) would lower the camera angle, and the focus is always on the girls and not on the bad men doing bad things.”

“I’m very mindful that when you see a woman’s body, you think about how you feel, and when you see a man’s body, you think about how the man feels. So I wanted to really make sure that we weren’t being exploitative and we were showing this perspective.”

“The Good Daughter” revolves around the sisters Charlotte “Charlie” and Samantha “Sam,” played by Meghann Fahy and Rose Byrne respectively, who are estranged as adults but reunite after one of them becomes unintentionally linked to a murder case. Together, the siblings must contend with the past in order to reconcile and embrace their futures.
Both Byrne and Fahy tell TODAY.com that they were drawn to the project because of the show’s focus on the strength of the characters, rather than on the abuse and suffering that they had endured.

“The show is about hope, and it’s about perseverance, and it’s about confronting the things that scare you, relieving yourself of unnecessary shame, and claiming the life that you really want to have for yourself and the people that you love,” Fahy says.

Byrne adds: “We wanted to celebrate the resilience of all situations like that and all people who survived these horrific events. ... A huge part of the conversation around when I signed on (was) how will this be dealt with? How will this be depicted?”

Both actors were tasked with embodying survivorship in different ways. For Byrne, Sam’s disability from a bullet wound to the head meant two months working on her gait with a physical therapist who rehabilitates similar patients in real life.
Fahy’s character Charlie, meanwhile, has kept a secret about the attack from everyone except her father, Rusty. Asked how she was able to bring that to life, Fahy points to the “responsibly run set.”

“There was a mental health specialist on set every day that was available to all of the actors and all of the crew if anybody needed support,” Fahy says, adding that Green “took very good care of everybody, so that created a super safe space.”
Slaughter hopes the show helps viewers, particularly those who have gone through trauma of their own, feel supported and safe.

“The most important line in the entire series and in the book is when Rusty says, ‘Whatever you did to survive is exactly what you should do,’” Slaughter explains. “That’s not a message women get often. We aren’t usually told, ‘You did the right thing.’ We’re told, ‘Why didn’t you do this? Why didn’t you do that?’”

On its face, “The Good Daughter” may seem like a quintessential thriller about women solving a crime in a small-town. But, according to Slaughter, it relies just as heavily on other warmer storytelling elements, like comedy and family dynamics.

“It’s so important to me to balance the light and dark,” the author says. “There are laugh-out-loud funny moments ... and that was so important for me to carry from the book into the show because, particularly being from the South ... there is that sensibility of even the worst situation you can find humor in.”
Slaughter adds that connection between the two sisters “propels you through the show as much as the whodunit.”
“At its heart, it’s about a family and this universal sense of dislocation and separation that we all feel as we grow up,” she says.
In fact, the least surprising but perhaps most satisfying aspect of the ending is that Sam and Charlie finally accept how much they need each other.

“The thing about writing about complicated, interesting women and not sentimentalizing them is that you have to know, as a viewer, that you trust the writer (is) going to leave you in a good place, and all my books end on a place of hope, and definitely the show ends on that hope too,” Slaughter says.

title: Ron Howard Reveals the 1 Person He Wishes He Could Have Met — And Why
summary: Actor and filmmaker Ron Howard reveals the inspiration behind his documentary “Avedon,” how the film parallels his own life and the person he wishes he’d met.
story: When the camera cuts, the interview isn’t over. With “Commercial Break,” TODAY.com catches up with guests between takes in Studio 1A for unfiltered moments and more questions.
If you’re wondering if Ron Howard is really the down-to-earth person everyone says he is, the answer is unequivocally yes.
Before we sit down to talk about Howard’s latest project, a documentary on acclaimed photographer Richard Avedon, we chat with Ice-T in the TODAY Lounge next to Studio 1A.
The pair strike up a conversation about Howard’s recent projects, including “Avedon” and the upcoming film “Alone At Dawn,” starring Anne Hathaway and Adam Driver.
Howard is called to set for his segment. As he leaves, Ice-T points after him and tells me, “He’s the OG.”

After getting his start on the “Andy Griffith Show” at the age of 6, Howard, 72, has maintained a steady show biz career, first in acting, then directing, for more 65 years. In the process, he’s earned two Oscars and dozens of nominations for films including “A Beautiful Mind,” “Frost/Nixon,” “Apollo 13,” “Parenthood,” “Cocoon” and “Hillbilly Elegy,” not to mention five Emmys for his work in television.

Howard has also earned a reputation for being one of the nicest guys in Hollywood. It’s one he fully lives up to when he catches up with TODAY.com backstage to talk about “Avedon,” the advice he gives his daughter, Bryce Dallas Howard, and the one person he’d have lunch with if he could.
This interview has been lightly edited for clarity.

Slowly, because he didn’t give a lot of interviews. Now we found two or three that were great and he’s very open. He’s very articulate, very funny, but he was guarded. For that reason, we had to dig through those archives to find him on camera, to find him telling his story.

We did find some old audio tapes that were damaged, but digitally now we’re able to repair those and make those something that we could really use in the film. So, there’s more of him in this documentary than you’ve ever seen before.
So, the man behind the camera slowly but surely, in my mind, became the central figure in this documentary and became really the story of a really great artist and a fascinating guy.

You’re really not alone. Again, he was very careful. So in certain circles, he’s known, he’s studied. I didn’t know much beyond the name, you know? He was a kind of a brand, but I had no idea the range of his work.
I also didn’t recognize how much he did do as a kind of a social documentarian. The civil rights movement, Andy Warhol, political unrest, Vietnam.

He was also, like a lot of good journalists, really interested in exposing hypocrisy through his lens. And he was pretty good at catching people off guard and revealing little insights that maybe weren’t so flattering.
We’re very different personalities, but I do see some parallels. And it is a love of the work and an excitement with what you can share, but also just what you get from it. I mean, he fed off of it.
I like to think that I have a little better work life balance than he was able to achieve. In the doc, he admits that that’s a regret of his.
